labels.name: area:build

labels.name: source:agent

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P5
labels.description: Agent surface and tooling keep up with what shipped

body:
Refs #3556. The maintainer's words on 2026-11-22: "should be small targeted shallow tests".

## What happens
`cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` prints "shared crate / workspace touched (crates/geometry/src/geo2d.rs): quick falls back to batch" when a diff changes a file of a shared crate, or a `Cargo.toml`. The plan is then the whole batch tier:
- PR #3353 (one change in `geo2d.rs`): 1102 steps, with 653 app test binaries;
- PR #3363 (a `Cargo.toml`): 1099 steps;
- PR #2515 (one post script and one table in `posting_files.rs`): 773 steps;
- PR #3472 (turning): 721 steps; a wave of three small PRs: 588 steps.

A build of all app test binaries takes 50 GB or more of disk and 30 to 50 minutes. Reviewers and workers then select steps by hand, and a hand selection lost a red test two times on 2026-11-22 (#3486, and the catalog case of #3478).

## Wanted
- The quick plan selects by the real use: for a changed file of a shared crate, the test binaries that reach the changed items (for example by the module, or by the public items that the diff changes), not each binary of each crate that depends on the crate.
- A limit with a clear message: when the selection is over a set number of steps, the plan prints the reason for each group, so that a person can see why.
- The example catalog suites are selected where a post or a toolpath changed (#3521).
- Tests in `xtask/` pin the selection for the four cases above.

Related: #3513, #3514, #3515 (slow tests), #3521 (catalog selection).

title: Drilling: check if a hole tilted some degrees from the tool axis is recognized as a Z hole and drilled along Z

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P1
labels.description: Unsafe or wrong output: gouge, collision, wrong G-code, crash, data loss; blocks a cut

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
Found by reading, in the second read of PR #3502. It is not a fault of that PR: the code is on `main`. **Nothing was run. This is a hypothesis.** The first step is a test that proves or disproves it.

## The hypothesis
The hole recognizers `recognize` and `recognize_cross` (`crates/motion/src/drilling/recognize.rs:87,97`) classify a hole from its wall facets with `WALL_NZ 0.7` and a circle fit with `FIT_TOL 0.02` (`recognize.rs:39,44`), in the setup frame.

A hole whose axis is tilted 2 degrees from the tool axis has a section that differs from a true circle by about 0.0006 r. That is far below the fit tolerance. Such a hole can pass as a Z hole. The drilling operation then drills along Z, and the drill cuts into the wall of the real hole. This is a gouge that passes with no message.

## Why P1
If the hypothesis is true, the posted program cuts in the wrong place and nothing blocks the post (the table: "a gouge or collision that passes").

## Wanted
1. A test with a part that has one hole tilted 2 degrees and one tilted 5 degrees from the tool axis (made from code, no model file). Assert what detection gives for each: a Z hole, a skipped hole with a name, or a cross hole.
2. If a tilted hole is taken as a Z hole: a tolerance on the angle of the axis (small, for example the angle at which the drill moves the wall by more than the tolerance of the operation over the hole depth), and a named skip for a hole outside it. Record the tolerance as a decision. Consider a parameter with a default (CAM choices are user parameters).
3. If the test shows that detection already refuses or skips the tilted hole: keep the test as a pin and close this issue with the commit.

Found while gating the #3173 PR on a Windows checkout with `core.autocrlf=true`. Environment-dependent test, not a behaviour change.

## What happens

A light-lane law test greps `AGENTS.md` for LF text. On a Windows checkout the file is checked out with CRLF, so the grep fails and the gate goes red for reasons that have nothing to do with the diff.

## What the fix needs

- The test (or the grep) must normalise line endings before it compares, so the law check is independent of `core.autocrlf`.
- The same pattern check is owed to any other test that greps a tracked text file byte-for-byte.

## Done means

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` is green on a Windows checkout with `core.autocrlf=true`, for the law test and any sibling grep test.

Observed on 2026-11-22 during the #3173 gate (PR #3552).

title: ui lib test binary dies with SIGSEGV on the Linux runner uma (post-merge run 45046106061, commit 87fb95f29)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Main is broken or a regression with no workaround; blocks a cut

labels.name: area:ui
labels.description: User interface and picking

labels.name: area:build
labels.description: Build, CI, release, tests

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
## What happened
Post-merge run 45046106061, second attempt, commit 87fb95f29 (the merge of PR #3363, the GPU compute seam), runner `uma`:

```
[1074] ui suites: lib
     (cwd ui) target/debug/build/camcraft-ui/4767f73a25f19268/out/camcraft_ui-4767f73a25f19268 --test-threads=16 (direct, from the build's cargo JSON artifacts)
     FAIL in 4s exit -1 (killed by signal 11 (SIGSEGV), core dumped)
  wall 42.2 min, 1100 step(s), 1 failed, 0 stalled
```

The other 1099 steps are green, the other 25 ui suites included. The log has no test name and no panic text: the process died 4 seconds after its start.

## What is known
- The run of 054c1e24b, a later commit that contains 87fb95f29, is green on the runner `wopr-2` (run 45050724895). The run of deb5364ee, the commit before 87fb95f29, is green on the runner `dude`.
- Thus the crash is not seen on each runner or in each run. The cause is not known. It can be the runner `uma`, or a fault that shows at intervals.
- 87fb95f29 is the first commit in which `camcraft-ui` links `camcraft-gpu` and `wgpu`. Check first if a ui lib test, or code that starts with the test binary, gets a GPU adapter or loads a graphics driver on a runner with no display.
- An earlier issue with the same sign: #2807 (closed), "ui test binary egui_app stops with SIGSEGV at intervals on the Linux runner".

## Why P2
A crash of a test binary makes the gate of `main` red at intervals. If the crash is in product code (a GPU probe at start), a user on Linux can get it too. Then the priority is P1.

## Wanted
- Find the test or the start code that crashes: run the ui lib binary on `uma` some times with `--test-threads=1` and with `CAMCRAFT_GPU_COMPUTE=off`, and read the core dump if the runner keeps it.
- If the cause is a GPU probe with no adapter or no display: the probe must give a named reason and the CPU path, never a crash (Prime Directive).
- A test that pins the fix, or a recorded reason if the fault is in the runner image.

title: The word Agie appears in the UI as if it were a feature or an operation

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
The maintainer reported this in chat on 2026-11-22: "the term AGIE has snuck thru in the UI in different parts where it doesnt belong. Agie is a machine, not a feature or operation.. it supports Klartext and iso wire edm."

What happens:
- Text that the user sees names Agie as if it were a feature, a post type or an operation rule. The machine name leaks into the product surface.
- The code names it the same way: `crates/app/src/posting_agie.rs`, `operation/agie_profile.rs` and `crates/post/src/agie/`.

Where it shows on `origin/main` at 054c1e24b (found by text search; the screens were not opened):
- `crates/app/src/posting.rs:62`: the wire post list holds the entry "Agie native wire EDM" (`posting_agie.rs:17`). It sits beside the neutral entries "Generic ISO Wire EDM" and "Sodick Wire EDM (Mark 21)".
- `assets/posts/agie-native.cps`: the post description reads "Agie native wire EDM: ...", and its parameter group reads "Agie technology".
- `crates/app/src/operation/agie_profile.rs` and `posting_agie.rs`: about 40 refusal messages start with "Agie requires ..." or "Agie supports ...". The user reads them in the post dialog. `AGIE_QN2` shows as a machine condition name.
- `crates/app/src/script/report.rs`, `posting_files.rs`, `posting_mounts.rs` and `posting_per_op.rs` also name Agie.

Expected:
- Agie is a machine. It belongs in the machine library: the machine file, its model name and its description.
- What the machine understands is a dialect of wire EDM output: Klartext and ISO. A post, a refusal or a parameter names the dialect or the capability. It does not name the machine.
- A refusal says what is wrong with the program ("The job needs a closed convex punch"), not which machine brand dislikes it.

Do not change:
- The posted output. Golden files stay equal.
- The machine file name and the model name `AGIECUT CLASSIC 2S` in the machine library. They are true statements about the machine.
- The attribution in `assets/ui/LICENSES.md`.

Check before the work:
- A project file can store the post name "Agie native wire EDM". A rename must keep old project files readable (alias or migration), or the issue records the break.
- Open PRs in the Agie stack (#3219, #2999, #2993 and the PRs below them) add more text of this kind. The fix must land in a way that those PRs can take.
- The post name can reach the command line, the MCP tools and the project file. Check each.

Done means:
- A search of `crates/ui` and of each user-visible string in `crates/app` finds the word Agie only in the machine library entry.
- The post list names the dialect (Klartext, ISO), not the machine.
- A test pins the post list and the refusal text without the word Agie.
- Posted output is unchanged (golden tests green).

Refs #2951.

Found in the review of PR #3532. The fault was on `main` before that PR (the crate `camcraft-gpu`, PR #3363).

## What happens
Each GPU call of the crate runs in an error scope. The crate does not install a handler for an uncaptured error, and none for a lost device, on the shared device. ## Wanted
- Install the two handlers when the shared device is made. A handler turns the GPU path off, logs the reason one time, and the callers get the CPU result.

body:
What happens: `read_back` in `crates/gpu/src/binning_gpu.rs` (lines 162-164 at `ef1572114`) polls the device with `wgpu::PollType::wait_indefinitely()`. A device that does not answer blocks the calling thread with no limit. Then the CPU fallback of the binning path does not run.

Expected: the poll has a time bound. A timeout is an `Err` with the reason, and the caller runs its CPU grid.

Evidence: found during the work on #2627. The new stock cut kernel (`crates/gpu/src/cut_gpu.rs`, PR for #2627) uses `PollType::Wait { submission_index: Some(at), timeout: Some(CUT_WAIT) }` and a bounded `recv_timeout` on the map callback. The binning path can use the same pattern.

Now there is no caller of `bin_facets` on a user path (#2621), so the defect has no user effect yet. It must be fixed before a caller is added.

Done means: `binning_gpu::read_back` waits for a bounded time, a timeout gives a named `Err`, and a test pins the named error text.

body:
Found in the second read of PR #3413 (head b38f0c12f). The label `bug` applies.

## What happens
A Face operation with protected items clips its rows by a keep-out. The keep-out of a level covers the heights from that level up to the clearance plane. A lower level gets the same keep-out or a larger one. Thus the blocked levels are always the lowest levels.

When one or more levels are blocked and one level stays clear, the operation generates. The face can stop above Cut Z in each place. The only sign is the note "blocked N facing level(s); the remaining levels stayed clear" (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/face_keep.rs:425-429`).

The note does not say that Cut Z was not reached. Nothing marks the operation "incomplete". The Prime Directive says: "If an operation can only be computed in part, mark it 'incomplete'."

The result is not a gouge. Material stays that the user expects to be removed.

## Wanted
- When a blocked level leaves the face above Cut Z, the operation says so in plain English with the depth that it reached, and it is marked "incomplete" (or refused: record the decision).
- A test with a keep-out that changes with Z (an item that is wider at a lower level) pins the message and the state.

title: Verifier: a rapid that the part-solid law convicts says "travels through stock (below the clearance plane)"

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:sim
labels.description: Stock simulation and verification

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
Found during the bounded search of #3319 (2026-11-22).

## What happens

The part-solid law (`crates/sim/src/verify/solid.rs:214-237`) judges each rapid against the part solid. When the tool body or its edge column meets the part, it pushes `Warning::RapidInStock { at: i }`.

That warning prints this text (`crates/sim/src/verify/types.rs:467-468`):

`rapid move N travels through stock (below the clearance plane, or at it below the stock top)`

The text is wrong for this case:
- The rapid can be vertical (a lift out of a pass, or a drop to a pass start).
- The rapid can be at or above the clearance plane at one end.
- The tool meets the part, not the uncut stock.

The user then reads it as a lateral G0 under the clearance plane. This is what happened in #3319.

## How to see it

Headless, `camcraft-cli mcp`, on `origin/main` 835556814 and on v0.25.0 (7e2a8119c):
1. `import_model` `testdata/models/fig8.step`; `add_tool` `EM-0800-4FL`; `fit_stock` box, sides `[5,5,5,5,0,2]`.
2. `edit_tool` `{"flute_len": 10}`.
3. `add_operation` "2D Offset" on the bottom face (Z 0), containment Outside. Clearance = Top of stock +10, Top = Top of stock +0, Bottom = Selection +1.5, Stepdown 10, Entry Helix r 1.6, `retract_z` null.
4. `generate`, then `verify`.

Result: `shank_hit` on moves 1406-1658 and 2194-2446 (the outer ring of levels 2 and 3), and `rapid_in_stock` on moves 1659, 2193 and 2447. Moves 1659 and 2447 are the vertical lifts to Z 32 at (-0.202, -33.998). Move 2193 is the vertical drop to Z 4 at the same point. Each lateral G0 of the posted program (a long-flute copy of the same path) is at Z 32.

The post is blocked, so the output is safe. Only the message is wrong.

## Done means

- A rapid that the part-solid law convicts gets a message that says the tool meets the part on a rapid, and that names the move.
- `rapids.rs` keeps its text for a rapid through the stock.
- A pin test in `crates/sim/tests/` shows the two texts on the two cases.
- The MCP `kind` string and the UI severity stay correct for the new text.

```rust
if let Err(e) = std::fs::write(path, &text) {
```

`std::fs::write` truncates the file first and then writes the new bytes. If the write stops before the end, the old project is gone and the new project is incomplete. This can occur when:

- the disk or the USB stick becomes full;
- the connection to a network share stops;
- the app or the computer stops during the write.

A cloud-sync client (OneDrive, Dropbox) or a backup tool can also read the file while it is half written, and copy the incomplete file to other computers.

All save routes use this function:

- the window: `State::save_project_path` (`crates/ui/src/state.rs:4716`);
- the MCP tool `save_project` and the script call `cam.save`: both go through `api::v_save` to `crate::project::save` (`crates/app/src/script/api.rs:49`).

I found this while I examined how CamCraft projects behave in shared and synced folders.

**Expected**

A failed save keeps the old `.camproj` file as it was. Other programs never see a half-written project file.

CamCraft already does this for machine files and for the fixture library. `machine::store::write_atomic` (`crates/app/src/machine/store.rs:104`) writes a temporary file in the same folder, flushes it, and renames it over the target. On a failure, it removes the temporary file, and the target stays as it was. `fixture_library/store.rs` has its own copy of the same steps (line 107).

**Steps to reproduce**

I found this by code inspection. I did not make a damaged file on a machine.

1. Open a project and save it to a `.camproj` file.
2. Read `project::save` in `crates/app/src/project/wire.rs`: the save opens the existing file with truncation before it writes the new text.
3. Any failure after step 2 leaves a short or empty file in the place of the old project.

**camcraft version and OS**

`main` at f14097855 (2026-11-22). The same code is in v0.24.0 and v0.25.0. Windows 11.

**Proposed change**

- `project::save` calls `machine::store::write_atomic`. Preferences, recent files, view settings and machine files already use this helper. No new module and no new copy.
- Two refusals of today stay:
  - a save into a folder that does not exist (the helper creates missing folders, so `project::save` checks first);
  - a save over a read-only `.camproj` file. On Linux and macOS, a rename replaces a read-only file, so `project::save` checks first.
- The file format and the saved text do not change. `PROJECT_VERSION` does not change.
- The browser build does not change. It gives the text to a download (`save_text`), not to a file path.
- On Windows, a rename can fail when another program holds the target file open. The save then reports the error, and the old file stays.

**Done means:** `project::save` replaces the target only through a rename of a complete, flushed temporary file in the same folder. A test shows that a failed save keeps the old `.camproj` byte for byte. A test shows that a good save leaves no temporary file. Tests show that a save into a missing folder and a save over a read-only file are refused, and that the old file stays. The `project_roundtrip` tests still pass.

I prepared this issue with Claude Code (an AI agent) and checked it.

title: xtask gate watchdog: kill a stalled step by process group or job object

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:build
labels.description: Build, CI, release, tests

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:medium
labels.description: One module or crate, a known pattern (issue-worker-medium)

labels.name: P7
labels.description: Owed polish and small fixes

body:
## Problem

The gate stall watchdog (#3303, PR #3489) kills a stalled step by its process tree. It reads the tree by parent pid (`ps` on Unix, `Win32_Process` on Windows), then kills each pid (`kill -KILL`, `taskkill /F /T`). This has three gaps:

- Between the read of the process list and the kill, a pid can be used again by a new process. The kill can then hit a wrong process. The window is small.
- A process that left the tree (a double fork, `setsid`) is not killed.
- In the capture path of `direct::cargo` (`xtask/src/direct.rs`), such a process can keep the stdout pipe open. Then `reader.join()` waits until that process ends.

## Change

- Unix: start each step child in its own process group (`std::os::unix::process::CommandExt::process_group(0)`), and kill the group (`kill -KILL -<pgid>`).
- Windows: put each step child in a job object, and end the job.
- Keep the present tree read for the list of the processes that were alive.

## Done means

- `xtask/src/watchdog.rs` kills by process group or job object.
- A test shows that a grandchild that left the tree by `setsid` (Unix) dies with the step.
- `cargo test -p xtask` and `cargo clippy -p xtask --all-targets -- -D warnings` are green.

Refs #3303

body:
Found by the second read of PR #3471 (comment 7081078749 on that PR). It is a reading of the code and of the usual control behaviour. It is NOT confirmed by a run, and no control ran it. The first step of the work is to confirm or to disprove it. If it is confirmed, this is wrong posted G-code and the priority goes to `P1`.

PR #3471 stops a G2/G3 block whose written end point equals its written start point (#3442). One more case stays: only the radial axis word changes between the start and the end of an arc, and the written start is within half an output step of the line through the centre. Then the written start and the written end have the same angle about the centre. A control that reads an equal angle as a full turn can cut a spiral of nearly one full turn.

By reading, this needs a radius below about 0.05 mm with mm output (3 decimals), or about 0.3 mm with inch output (4 decimals).

## Necessary work
1. A recorded input with such an arc for the mm case and the inch case. Post it with `fanuc.cps` and `linuxcnc.cps`. Show the blocks.
2. Find from public documentation of the two controls how each reads an arc whose start and end have the same angle and different radii.
3. If the block is unsafe: extend the guard of `crates/post/src/post/arc_guard.rs` (for example, check the turn direction and the sweep from the WRITTEN words, and post a linear move when the written sweep is not the sweep of the record). Add the case to the table test over all posts.

labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
## What is wanted

A Part (part-off) operation has no parameter for the position of the kerf. Since #3452, the whole kerf of the blade is always on the waste side of the parting plane (the end face of the finished part).

Some shops need the kerf in another position. Two examples:

- The operator leaves a facing allowance on the back of the part, for a second-side facing operation. The kerf is then a set distance into the waste side, or the plane is a set distance into the part.
- The blade is centred on the plane because a later operation faces the part to its length.

The product rule is that a strategy choice is a user parameter with a default. Add a "kerf position" parameter (or a "back stock" allowance) to the Part operation.

## Done means

- The default is the #3452 behaviour: the whole kerf is behind the end face. Existing projects post the same program.
- The parameter is in the project file, the operation page and MCP, through `EditOperationParams` (undoable).
- The gouge law of #3452 (`part_kerf_refusal`) judges the kerf against the part that the parameter keeps. A setting that puts the blade into material the part must keep is refused by name.
- Tests pin each setting on the case of #3452 (end face Z-70, 3 mm blade, orientation 2).

Refs #3452

labels.name: P1
labels.description: Unsafe or wrong output: gouge, collision, wrong G-code, crash, data loss; blocks a cut

labels.description: 3+2, 5-axis, rotary

labels.name: area:post

body:
Found by a read of `origin/main` (f14097855) on 2026-11-22, after a note in the second read of PR #3421. It is NOT confirmed by a run: the first step of the work is a test that posts such a program.

## What the code does
A program has two operations in one setup: first a five-axis operation that leans the tool (5-Axis Contour, Flow, Swarf), then a 3-axis operation with the tool upright.

1. The tilted section ends with the tool still tilted. Its exit rapids keep the pose (`crates/motion/src/multiaxis/stamp.rs`, near line 210).
2. `dump()` in `crates/post/src/post/mod.rs` keeps the state `tilted` for one operation only (lines 430 and 520-541). The first upright move of the next operation gets no angles.
3. `assets/posts/fanuc.cps`: `endPreamble` (786-838) resets `tcpmOn` and `lastA/B/C` in the script only. `startPreamble` (742) writes `G49` only. No block writes `A0` or `B0`. `retractHome` is `G28 Z0` with no rotary axis.
4. `assets/posts/doosan-dnm.cps`: `endPreamble` (873-905) resets `lastA/B/C` only. `startPreamble` writes `G49` only.

Result, by reading: the posted program has no rotary word between the last tilted move and the first cut of the upright operation. The machine stays at the last tilted angles, and the 3-axis operation cuts with the tool or the table tilted. That is wrong posted G-code (a gouge or a collision), and no check stops it:

- `first_traverse_posed` judges only the first operation of the post order (`crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs:3325`).
- No check compares the pose at the end of one operation with the start of the next.

## Posts that are safe, by the same read
- `tormach.cps` writes `G53 G0 Z` and `G0 A0` at the first upright move of a section (718-775).
- `mach4.cps` writes `G00 A<zero> C<zero>` when the stored lean is different (about 575-625).
- The posts that refuse a tilted move cannot post the first operation.

## Necessary work
1. A test that posts a tilted operation followed by an upright operation with `fanuc.cps` on `tilthead.mch` and with `doosan-dnm.cps`. It shows the blocks between the two sections. If the program states the angles, close this issue with that evidence.
2. If it does not: each section that follows a tilted section states the rotary position before its first approach, at a safe height (the pattern of PR #3421 for the opening of a tilted section, and of `tormach.cps`). The same for a tool change between the two, and for the same tool in the two operations.
3. A check in the app: an upright operation after a tilted one posts only when the return to upright is stated, else a refusal with a diagnostic.
4. The same test for each post that supports a rotary axis.

Context pack: `.claude/tmp/context/stale-tilt-between-sections.md` (local). PR #3421 changes the same code (`post/mod.rs` `dump`, `stamp.rs`): stack on it.

Refs #3300

title: Generators can emit arcs with a chord under 1 um

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P7
labels.description: Owed polish and small fixes

body:
Refs #3442

## Problem

The 2D generators can emit an arc whose chord is shorter than 1 micrometre. No arc path in the CL or in the motion crate has a minimum chord or a minimum sweep. After #3442, each shipped post writes such an arc as a straight move or as no block, so the posted program is safe. But the toolpath, the simulation and the CL file still carry an arc that no output format can show.

## Sites (found by a read, not by a run)

- `crates/cl/src/cl/path.rs` `push_arc` and `push_arc_in`: the only test is that the end differs from the start. There is no chord floor.
- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/fillet.rs`: the sweep is at least 0.5 degrees and the radius floor is `MIN_BLEND_RADIUS = 0.01` mm. The chord can therefore be about 0.09 um.
- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/arcs.rs` `fit_arcs_sided`: the split pieces are index-based. A piece over clustered input vertices can possibly have a sub-micrometre chord. This is not tested.
- `crates/motion/src/entry_arc.rs` `arc_lead_swept`: the sweep has no floor in this code. Where the `arc_sweep` parameter is validated was not read.
- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/arc_biarc.rs`: no chord floor.

The rings already have a floor: `MIN_ARC_CHORD = 0.01` mm in `crates/motion/src/ring_zig.rs`, used by `ring_walk` and `push_zig_ring`.

## Done means

- Each arc-emitting generator emits a straight segment (or nothing) in place of an arc whose chord is under one law, for example `MIN_ARC_CHORD`.
- A test pins each site with a fixture that would emit a sub-micrometre arc today.
- The CL input law does not change: a short arc in an outside `.cnc` file stays legal input (#3442).

labels.name: P5

body:
From the merge-order analysis of 2026-11-22. AGENTS.md, "Heavy lanes at review" (#2568): the author runs `cargo xtask gate heavy` on the final head of each PR whose diff reaches a heavy lane. One run of the motion and app lanes takes 60 to 70 minutes, and only one heavy build can run at a time on a machine. For a wave of 9 PRs that reach the lanes, this is about 12 hours.

## Proposal (the maintainer decides; this changes AGENTS.md)
A wave of PRs that the planner puts in one group can use ONE heavy run on the trial tree of the wave: the current `main` with each PR of the wave merged. The run covers each PR, because the tree contains each diff. The result is recorded on each PR of the wave (the tree hash, the lanes, the counts). If the run is red, the red step is attributed to a PR, that PR leaves the wave, and the run starts again for the rest.

Rules that stay:
- "Not run" is never a pass.
- A PR that merges alone keeps the rule of today.
- The release tier at the cut stays the final check.

## Necessary work
1. A decision entry in `docs/decisions/` with the maintainer's answer.
2. The text of AGENTS.md ("Heavy lanes at review") and of the `gate`, `merge-ready` and `review-prs` skills.
3. `cargo xtask gate heavy` accepts a trial tree and prints the list of the PR heads that it covers.

The PR has `Process change: yes`.

[q07-router.camproj](https://github.com/mkinney/Camcraft/blob/qa-artifacts/qa/round2-20261122/q07-router-mdf/q07-router.camproj), [q07-router.step](https://github.com/mkinney/Camcraft/blob/qa-artifacts/qa/round2-20261122/q07-router-mdf/q07-router.step), posted [q07-router.nc](https://github.com/mkinney/Camcraft/blob/qa-artifacts/qa/round2-20261122/q07-router-mdf/q07-router.nc) (operation ProfileCutout from line 372; the tabbed level at lines 456-490); agent report [REPORT.md](https://github.com/mkinney/Camcraft/blob/qa-artifacts/qa/round2-20261122/q07-router-mdf/REPORT.md) problem 8.

## What happens

The part spans WCS Z 0 (front) to Z -70 (back face, with a 1 x 45° head chamfer at Z -70..-69); the bar runs on to Z -84. Op7_Part_Off: kind `part`, tool GT-0300 (3.0 mm wide grooving blade, orientation 2), `bottom_z` = bottom of model. Posted (q03-turn-shaft.nc lines 1813-1858):

```
(T0404 Parting_3mm - GROOVING BLADE ORIENTATION 2)
G0 X34
G0 Z-71.5
G1 X30 Z-71.5 F0.025
...
G1 X0 Z-71.5 F0.025
```

In the same program the groove finish passes show the convention since #641: the posted Z is the blade's -Z corner. The 2.5 mm O-ring groove Z -33.75..-36.25 is cut with the 2 mm blade at Z -36.25 and -35.75 (blade spans -36.25..-33.75, exact), and the 3 mm relief Z -17..-20 at Z -20 and -19. So the part-off blade at Z -71.5 spans **Z -71.5..-68.5**: it cuts 1.5 mm into the finished part's back face and removes the head chamfer. The part comes off 68.5 mm long instead of 70.

`verify` reports no warning for the operation (the lathe stock sim does not judge turning: "a turning program is cut by the field eye about its fitted spindle ... not judged here; the revolved verdict at generation stands"). The workaround the agent tried, `bottom_z` = bottom of model - 1.5, is refused: "nothing to part - the parting plane stands off the end of the bar" (the bar runs 14 mm further).

The part-off blade's +Z flank stands at or behind the part's end plane (posted -Z corner at Z -73.0 for this 3 mm blade), or the operation is refused; a part-off that cuts into the part is a gouge and holds the post.

body:
Found by the QA swarm round 2 (#2582): four of the five agent runs on CamCraft **v0.25.0** (Linux x86_64 release, headless MCP) lost time or a feature to this.

## What happens

`list_operation_types` prints each kind's fields with defaults and one note: "Fields absent from the defaults are optional and off; set them in a params patch to turn them on." It never names those fields. In v0.25.0:

| kind | fields listed | accepted but not listed (found by the agents through serde errors or not at all) |
|---|---|---|
| pocket, face, contour, ... | pocket: bottom_z, clearance_z, climb, entry, feed, helix_radius, optimal_load, plunge_feed, stepdown, stepover, stock_to_leave, strategy, top_z | `tilt` (the 3+1 / 3+2 index, guide "Indexed work"), `rest` (RestDto: previous_tool_diameter, ...) |
| wire_contour | bottom_z, side, top_z | `condition` (**required**: add_operation refuses without it), `taper_deg`, `start`, `skims`, `tabs` {count, width, at, cutoff_condition}, `capture` |
| plasma_profile | bottom_z, clearance_z, comp, lead_in, lead_out, overburn, reversed, small_hole_dia, small_hole_feed, top_z | `feed`, `kerf`, `pierce_delay`, `pierce_height`, `cut_height` (unset, the posted plasma program had no F word and no M207/M208/M209) |
| drill | ... cycle ... | `cross` (see #3448); `cycle`'s values (auto, spot, drill, peck, tap, bore, back_bore, floating_tap, ream, fine_bore) |

Enum fields (`cycle`, `strategy`, `entry`, `side`, finish3d `pattern`) are typed only `"string"`.

Effect seen in the runs: q05 never found `tilt`, so it programmed the 4th-axis faces as manual re-clamp setups instead of indexed A moves; q06 had to probe `condition`, `taper_deg`, `capture` and the plasma feed/pierce fields one error at a time; q04 found `rest` only from a serde error.

## Expected

Each kind lists every field it accepts (with type, unit, default or "off", and the allowed values of an enum), so an agent can discover a feature from the tool alone. #3217 covers the wire-only part of this and the camcraft-mcp skill.

## Evidence

Agent reports: [q05 REPORT.md](https://github.com/mkinney/Camcraft/blob/qa-artifacts/qa/round2-20261122/q05-4axis/REPORT.md) (confusing-tools 4), [q06 REPORT.md](https://github.com/mkinney/Camcraft/blob/qa-artifacts/qa/round2-20261122/q06-wire-plasma/REPORT.md) problem 2, [q04 REPORT.md](https://github.com/mkinney/Camcraft/blob/qa-artifacts/qa/round2-20261122/q04-vcarve-sign/REPORT.md) problem 4, [q01 REPORT.md](https://github.com/mkinney/Camcraft/blob/qa-artifacts/qa/round2-20261122/q01-2d-plate/REPORT.md) (enum values).

Done means: list_operation_types names every accepted field of every kind, optional ones marked as such, with enum values listed; a test fails when a params struct gains a field the listing does not show.

The Tormach 24R machine file states no coolants. A user who sets an operation's coolant to **Off** (the right choice on a dry router) cannot post:

On a machine whose coolant list is empty (or that states no Flood), Off posts: it writes no coolant word, which is what the post writes for Flood there anyway. Related but different: #3124 (hobby router files start new operations on Flood).

body:
Found by the QA swarm round 2 (#2582), brief q04, CamCraft **v0.25.0** (Linux x86_64 release) with SolidCraft **v0.46.2**; minimised by hand.

## What happens

A plate 160 x 70 x 15 mm with a 140 x 50 x 4 mm pocket cut from the top (pocket wall at X = 70) and one Ø6 through hole on that wall (axis at X = 70, Y = 0, so half the hole is 15 mm deep and half 11 mm deep). SolidCraft measures it exactly (volume 139632.434 mm³ = 168000 - 28000 - 9π·13; area 30984.496 mm², also exact; 13 faces, closed).

Both imports refuse it:

```
import_model (.step): corrupt STEP: solid #528 'Body1' could not be tessellated: machining mesh: face 12 capped at 3.307e0 mm sag, tolerance 5e-3 mm - re-export the model, or import an STL
import_model (.sc):   Solidcraft design refused: machining mesh: face 12 capped at 3.307e0 mm sag, tolerance 5e-3 mm
```

Face 12 is the hole's one cylindrical face, whose top edge steps from Z 15 to Z 11 across the wall. 3.307 mm is about the hole's whole span, so the tessellator seems to give up on that face rather than miss by a little. In the full q04 design (R8 and R2 fillets added) the STEP imported but the .sc did not.

## Expected

The model imports like any closed solid, or the refusal says which face and why in terms a user can act on ("re-export" does not help: the file is valid).

## Repro files

- Minimal SolidCraft script [hole-on-pocket-wall.json](https://github.com/mkinney/Camcraft/blob/qa-artifacts/qa/round2-20261122/verify/hole-on-pocket-wall.json) (`solidcraft-cli run hole-on-pocket-wall.json --out x.step`), and its outputs [hole-on-pocket-wall.step](https://github.com/mkinney/Camcraft/blob/qa-artifacts/qa/round2-20261122/verify/hole-on-pocket-wall.step), [hole-on-pocket-wall.sc](https://github.com/mkinney/Camcraft/blob/qa-artifacts/qa/round2-20261122/verify/hole-on-pocket-wall.sc).

body:
Found by the QA swarm round 2 (#2582), brief q04 (sign plate), CamCraft **v0.25.0** Linux x86_64 release over headless MCP; reproduced by hand on the same build.

## What happens

The part is a plate 160 x 70 x 15 mm (R8 corners) with a 140 x 50 x 4 mm centred pocket and two Ø6 through holes at X = ±70 (on the pocket wall). A 2D Contour, side **outside**, picked on the outer chain, top = top of model, bottom = bottom of model (Z 0), stepdown 3, 4 tabs, Router up-cut 6 mm, generates with `status: ok`, `warnings: 0` and only this note:

```
depth: the ring at (72.067, -37.999) ends at its floor Z 7.061 - the part is solid below it; levels below skipped (6.000, 3.000, 2.000, 0.000)
```

The point (72.067, -37.999) is 3 mm outside the plate edge (Y = -35), the tool-centre ring. Nothing of the part is below it. The posted program stops at Z 7.061 (G54 Z-8.939 with the WCS at the stock top), so the plate is never cut free and none of the 4 tabs are made. `verify` says `ok: true` with no findings. With `stock_to_leave: 0.02` the false floor moves by exactly +0.02 (Z 7.081 at (72.067, -38.019)). Same result with `tab_count: 0` and with the bottom outer chain picked.

The generate also takes 133 s for this one contour (re-run on len, 8 cores; the agent saw 3-6 min, so its MCP calls timed out at 3 min).

## Expected

The contour cuts every level down to Z 0 and makes the 4 tabs, or names a real reason the levels are skipped as a warning, not an ok status.

## Evidence / repro files

- Project: [q04-vcarve-sign-posted-5ops.camproj](https://github.com/mkinney/Camcraft/blob/qa-artifacts/qa/round2-20261122/q04-vcarve-sign/q04-vcarve-sign-posted-5ops.camproj) (operation "Contour Cutout"), model [q04-vcarve-sign.step](https://github.com/mkinney/Camcraft/blob/qa-artifacts/qa/round2-20261122/q04-vcarve-sign/q04-vcarve-sign.step), posted [q04-vcarve-sign.nc](https://github.com/mkinney/Camcraft/blob/qa-artifacts/qa/round2-20261122/q04-vcarve-sign/q04-vcarve-sign.nc) (lines 6751-6824).
- MCP: `open_project {"path": ".../q04-vcarve-sign-posted-5ops.camproj"}`, `generate {"name": "Contour Cutout"}` gives the note above.
- Agent report: [REPORT.md](https://github.com/mkinney/Camcraft/blob/qa-artifacts/qa/round2-20261122/q04-vcarve-sign/REPORT.md) problem 8.

How bad: no gouge, but a wrong program passes as ok: the operator finds an uncut plate (7 mm left) and no tabs.

Done means: the q04 project's "Contour Cutout" generates every level to Z 0 with its 4 tabs (pinned by a test on this model or a smaller one with a hole on the pocket wall), and a skipped level that is not truly blocked by the part is never reported as only a note.

title: Fanuc inch post can write a full-circle G03 for a short arc

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P1
labels.description: Unsafe or wrong output: gouge, collision, wrong G-code, crash, data loss; blocks a cut

labels.name: area:post
labels.description: Post processors and G-code

labels.name: in-review
labels.description: Fix pushed on a branch with an open PR; merges at the next cut

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
The native `post` command accepts two short counterclockwise arcs and writes two G03 blocks with coincident start and end XY coordinates. Both blocks have a nonzero center offset. A control that treats these blocks as full circles can cut a circle instead of a short stroke.

I reproduced this with CamCraft `post 0.25.0 (boa_engine)` and the original `assets/posts/fanuc.cps`. The post, CL reader and post script match main at `b44a422bb`. I checked the generated file. No controller or machine ran it.

## Reproduce

Save the following synthetic input as `tiny.cnc`. The coordinates in the intermediate file use micrometres.

```
; HSMW-CNC v1
PARAM OperationName Arc precision witness
PARAM SpindleSpeed 6000
PARAM WorkOffset 1
PARAM OriginX 0
PARAM OriginY 0
PARAM OriginZ 0
PARAM ToolDiameter 4
PARAM ClearancePlane 18
PARAM RetractPlane 18
PARAM TopOfStock 6
TOOL 1 EM-0400-2FL
SECTION Arc precision witness
Rapid X 18123 Y 5432 Z 18000
Plunge X 18123 Y 5432 Z 5500 F 45000
Arc CCW X 18123 Y 5433 Z 5500 F 180000 I 10123 J 5432
Arc CCW X 18123 Y 5434 Z 5500 F 180000 I 10123 J 5432
Rapid X 18123 Y 5434 Z 18000
ENDSECTION
```

Run `cargo run -p camcraft-post --bin post -- --units inch assets/posts/fanuc.cps tiny.cnc tiny.nc`.

The input Y positions are 5432, 5433 and 5434 µm. Each arc has a sweep of about 0.00716°. In the NC file, the preceding position and both arc endpoints are X0.7135 Y0.2139. Each arc reads:

```text
G03 X0.7135 Y0.2139 Z0.2165 I-0.315 J0. F7.09
```

The command exited successfully. It reported 13 mapped records, nine blocks and zero swallowed records.

## Expected

The post must preserve the short motion at the selected precision or refuse it with a diagnostic. It must distinguish a short arc from an intended full turn. Pin this input through the native post command. Also check a representable short arc and a genuine full circle.

Found while testing #1869. A check in the new sketch generator protects that feature. The native post also accepts intermediate files from other sources. #2191 concerned the radius-word mode and a different rounding failure.

Suggested labels are `bug`, `P1`, `area:post`, `effort:high`, and `source:agent`.

body:
`app heavy: shared_face_bodies_finish` took 739 s in the release gate (`8643d9bb7`).
It is the longest step of the release gate.

We timed all six release bands in `crates/app/tests/shared_face_bodies_finish.rs` on 6 parallel workers (wall 891.67 s, sum 1,685.07 s):
- `band_6_of_6`: 891.66 s (52.9%)
- `band_4_of_6`: 755.60 s (44.8%)
- `band_5_of_6`: 21.72 s (1.3%)
- `band_3_of_6`: 6.53 s (0.4%)
- `band_1_of_6`: 5.43 s (0.3%)
- `band_2_of_6`: 4.13 s (0.2%)

Bands 4 and 6 take 1,647.26 s (97.8% of the binary).
Bands 1, 2, 3, and 5 finish in 37.81 s total (2.2%).
Even at `--test-threads=2`, Bands 4 and 6 already run at the same time.
Splitting this file into six binaries or sharding its six existing tests does not lower the 739 s floor.

What to do:
1. Replace the equal-height `BANDS = 6` split in `crates/app/tests/shared_face_bodies_finish.rs` with explicit Z-offset band edges.
2. Cut the Band 4 and Band 6 Z ranges into narrower sub-bands so no single band exceeds 150 s in release.
3. Update `the_3d_finish_bands_tile_the_whole_span` to verify gap-free coverage across all band edges from `top_of_model` to `bottom_of_model`.
4. Keep `the_3d_finish_band_split_levels_move_within_stepdown_and_links_cross_edge` and every gouge and `shank_hit` assertion unchanged.

Done means:
- Every heavy band test in `crates/app/tests/shared_face_bodies_finish.rs` finishes under 150 s in release.

title: Gate: shard long queued test binaries by libtest --list names in xtask

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:build
labels.description: Build, CI, release, tests

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P6
labels.description: Accepted enhancement, not scheduled

body:
In `xtask/src/budget.rs` and `xtask/src/queue.rs`, a 16-core gate run uses `lane_limit(16) = 8` lanes and `per_lane(16, 8) = 2` (`--test-threads=2`).
Every queued step stays locked to 2 threads, even when the other 7 lanes sit idle.

Splitting long binaries into more `crates/*/tests/*.rs` files has a high cost:
- `crates/app/tests/` already has 542 binaries (median 82.6 MB debug, up to 134 MB for `shared_face_bodies_finish`; 24-53 MB release).
- `camcraft-motion --lib` cannot move its slow unit tests into `tests/*.rs`. All seven slow files import private `pub(super)` or `#[cfg(test)]` hooks (`OPEN_INSET`, `PEAK`, `PEAK_LEN`, `plan_from_air`, `cut_lane`, `plan_all_lanes`, `hsm_passes`).

What to do:
1. After the `--no-run` prebuild in `xtask`, locate the compiled binary for each queued step whose `timings.tsv` duration exceeds a threshold (for example 120 s).
2. Run `<exe> --list` (with `--ignored` for heavy steps) to collect the exact test names. This captures macro-generated tests such as `band!` in `shared_face_bodies_finish.rs` that regex-based `scan::test_fns` misses.
3. Partition the test names into shards and enqueue each shard with `--exact <names...>`.
4. Use one test per shard for heavy binaries with few tests. For large targets, keep each shard command line under 16 KB for Windows's 32 KB `CreateProcessW` cap (`camcraft-motion --lib` active names total 35,086 chars).
5. Name shards `<step name> [k/n]`. This keeps `select::name_matches` (`--only "<step name>"`), `--failed`, and `lanes::target_key` (`ISOLATED`) working cleanly.
6. Sum `<step name> [k/n]` durations by base step name when reading `timings.tsv` so sharded binaries stay sharded on later runs.
7. Order individual shards longest-first from their own `timings.tsv` rows.
8. Assert in `xtask` that the union of shard test names equals `<exe> --list` with zero missing or duplicate tests.

Done means:
- Multi-test heavy binaries fan out across all available release-gate lanes with zero new `tests/*.rs` binaries and zero Gate-map changes.
- `xtask` unit tests pin `--list` union coverage, command-line length bounds, and `timings.tsv` aggregation.
- `cargo test -p xtask` and `cargo clippy -p xtask --all-targets -- -D warnings` pass.

## Goal

- Define an append-only rolling JSONL file (`failures.jsonl`, capped at 500 runs) that records commit SHA, UTC time, changed file paths, failed test names, and step durations.

`xtask` reads and appends `failures.jsonl`, ranks tests by co-failure rate divided by duration with recency and new-test boosts, handles renamed files and corrupt lines safely, and passes unit tests.

title: Five-axis approach feed turns the rotaries while it descends to the first contact

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: claimed
labels.description: An agent is working on this - see the claim comment

labels.name: area:multiaxis
labels.description: 3+2, 5-axis, rotary

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

labels.name: P7
labels.description: Owed polish and small fixes

body:
## What happens

Found while working #3300. The 5-axis stamp (`crates/motion/src/multiaxis/stamp.rs`) gives the approach feed the lean of its end station. The approach feed starts upright at the clearance and ends at the first contact. So the rotaries turn during the descent to the stock.

Posted on `assets/machines/tilthead.mch` with `assets/posts/fanuc.cps` (the #3300 case, 5-Axis Contour on a spherical cap, clearance 20 mm, G54 at Z 50):

```text
G43.4 H01
G00 Z-30.
G00 X0. Y-3.84 Z-30. A0. B0.
G01 X-0.776 Y-3.149 Z-47.314 A13.313 B15.42 F100
```

The G01 block turns A by 13.3 degrees and B by 15.4 degrees while the tool moves 17 mm down to the part. Flow5D and Swarf show the same opening (A21.6 B9.8, and A32.5 B17.9).

This is not new with #3300. On a machine with no stated rotary rate, main posts the same G01 block today. #3300 only makes the start angle known (A0 B0 at the clearance).

## Expected

The rotaries go to the first lean at a safe height, then the tool approaches the part with a constant pose: retract, rotate, then approach. A rotary move near the stock is the exception, and a judgment states why it is safe.

## Notes

- `cam.verify()` passes this program. It is not proven that the turn gouges. This issue asks for a decision on the approach law.
- A fix changes the stamp's pose law for the approach stations (a held lead-in pose, or a rapid that turns at the clearance). It changes posted G-code, so the safety floor applies.

Done means: the opening approach of a leaning 5-axis path does not turn a rotary below the clearance, or a decision records why the current law is safe. A test pins the chosen law with the tilt-head machine.

body:
The AI chat panel already has a scripted test transport (`ScriptedTransport` in `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/ai_chat/mod.rs`) and about 25 tests: tool dispatch through the inbox, one Ctrl+Z per AI turn, cancel, offline-only policy, confirmation gates, the round cap, local vs cloud tool sets. Those scripts are hand-written: each `tool_use` is the shape the test author expected.

What is not covered: the shapes REAL models send. Local models (Ollama / LM Studio / llama.cpp, e.g. qwen3-coder) and cloud models differ in argument JSON (numbers as strings, extra or missing fields, unit words, several tool calls in one reply, a call to a tool from the other tool set). A change to the tool schema or the argument parser can break a real model's workflow while every scripted test stays green.

Proposal:
1. A recorded fixture format: one JSON file per conversation (user messages, each model reply with its raw tool calls, the expected document diff after each turn). The QA swarm brief q08 (AI panel with a local model) saves exactly this transcript per run.
2. A `ReplayTransport` (beside `ScriptedTransport`) that plays a recorded reply sequence back, and one test per fixture that drives the real panel and asserts the document after each turn (operations, key parameters, one undo step per turn, refusals shown).
3. Start with three recorded workflows: "add a finishing pass for the pocket walls" (local model), "make it climb with 0.2 mm stepdown" (edit one op only), and "delete every operation" (confirmation gate holds).

No network in the test: replay only. Recording happens outside the gate (QA runs).

**Done means:** a `ReplayTransport` and fixture format in the ui test tree, three recorded fixtures (at least one from a local model), each with a test that fails when the tool argument parser or dispatch changes the outcome, and a short note in the camcraft-mcp skill or docs on how to record a new fixture.

body:
PathPilot Mill (`UM10587` Ch. 10) and the LinuxCNC G-code reference document extended work offsets (`G54.1 P1`..`P500`), feed per revolution (`G95`), constant surface speed (`G96 D S`), and spindle-synchronized threading (`G33 Z K`). On LinuxCNC, `G96` measures radius strictly from active WCS `X0` (never `Y`), and `G95`, `G96`, and `G33` require spindle encoder feedback (`motion.spindle-speed-in`), which servo-spindle mills such as the Tormach 770MX (`rigid_tapping: true`) provide.

Verify these behaviours on PathPilot Hub (770MX SIM) and then extend `assets/posts/tormach-mill-turn-spindle.cps` and machine capability checks:

- Record PathPilot Hub readings for `G54.1 P` index mapping (`P1`..`P6` vs `G54`..`G59`, `P7`..`P9` vs `G59.1`..`G59.3`, `P10`..`P255`), `G43 H` persistence across WCS changes, `G95`, `G96 D S`, and `G33 Z K` in Mill mode.
- Widen `workOffsetMax` and `workOffsetName(n)` in the part-in-spindle post to emit `G54.1 P<n>` up to `255` (`crates/post/src/post/work_offset.rs::MAX_BOUND`) once verified.
- Enable `G96 D<cap> S<vc>` with `G95` only on X-axis stations of machines with spindle encoder feedback and an explicit RPM clamp `D = min(machine.spindle_max, tool.max_rpm, setup.workholding_max_rpm)`. Always restore `G97` and `G94` at section end.
- Refuse `G96` on Y-axis stations and refuse `G95`, `G96`, and `G33` on machines without spindle encoder feedback.
- Enable `G33 Z K` threading when the thread hand's spindle direction matches the station's allowed direction, and refuse any mismatch by name.

Done means: PathPilot Hub readings are recorded in the PR or decision file, golden `.nc` tests pin `G54.1 P`, gated `G96`/`G95`, and `G33` output, and refusal tests pin Y-axis `G96`, non-encoder machines, unclamped CSS, and mismatched thread hand.

body:
In part-in-spindle turning, the collet nose sits at the top of the stock (`Z = -stock_stickout_mm`) and every stationary lathe tool block rides together on the mill table. A cut or rapid can drive the active tool into the collet nose, or drive the spinning stock and collet into a neighbouring tool block.

Extend turning verification (`crates/app/src/operation/turning_holder_steel.rs`, `crates/app/src/fixture_struck.rs`, `crates/tools/src/lathe_holder.rs`):

- Model the collet nose and spindle body (`Machine::spindle_d`, `Machine::spindle_len`) as revolved steel above the stock stick-out, and refuse any active tool or holder contact with `Warning::FixtureHit`.
- Support optional table positions and bounding boxes on each table tool station.
- While one station moves (rapids and feeds), check every other station's box against the swept envelope of the stock, part, collet nose, and spindle body. Emit a blocking `Warning::FixtureHit` on contact.
- Follow the unstated-limit law: when station positions or block boxes are not stated, emit a named note on the operation stating that inter-station block clearance was not judged.
- Add a non-blocking warning note when stock stick-out exceeds `3 * diameter` without tailstock support.

Done means: verifier tests prove blocking `Warning::FixtureHit` findings for collet-nose strikes and neighbouring gang-block strikes, prove clear paths pass, and confirm the not-judged note when station positions are omitted.

Two such helices can stand side by side. Their arcs then cross in XY at a shared depth, and `verify::crossed_pairs` names the pair.

**Where it shows.** `crates/motion/tests/pass_start_levels.rs`, the band case (stock 84 x 24, a round part of radius 15, tool radius 4, Helix entry radius 1.5):
- Outside, step 3: the first descent helix (moves 2-5) and the next re-entry helix (moves 16-19) cross.
- Inside, step 4: moves 3/5 and 13/15 cross.

The test `the_start_side_plan_posts_no_crossing_feeds` checks only the planar feeds for this reason.

**Not a gouge.** Both helices stay in the certified area. The second one bores where the first one cut already. The defect is the warning that the user sees, and an entry that does not use the cut column.

**Done means.** A re-entry whose helix would overlap an earlier helix at the same depth uses that cleared column (or moves its site), and the crossing law finds no helix pair. A test pins the band case above.

title: chore(process): merge-ready and needs-rework never coexist on a PR

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:build
labels.description: Build, CI, release, tests

labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:low
labels.description: Mechanical, one file, no new logic (issue-worker-low)

labels.name: P5
labels.description: Agent surface and tooling keep up with what shipped

body:
The maintainer said in chat on 2026-11-22: "PR's with merge-ready cannot have needs-rework at the same time.."

## The rule today
`AGENTS.md`, "Only collaborators' reviews count": a PR whose current head has a collaborator's change request and also `merge-ready` (or `merge-ready` with `needs-rework`) is a disagreement. `/merge-ready` reports it. "No agent removes a label. The two collaborators decide on the PR."

## The new rule
1. `merge-ready` and `needs-rework` are never on the same PR.
2. The person or agent that sets one of the two labels removes the other label in the same step, with one comment that says why.
3. A disagreement between two collaborators on the same head: `needs-rework` stays and `merge-ready` is removed. An open change request wins. The collaborator who set `merge-ready` gets the comment.
4. This replaces the text "No agent removes a label" for these two labels.

## Files to change
- `AGENTS.md`: the rule "Only collaborators' reviews count" (the disagreement items) and the "Review labels" table.
- `.claude/skills/merge-ready/SKILL.md`
- `.claude/skills/review-prs/SKILL.md` and the `PR-reviewer` agent file, where they set a review label.
- `.claude/skills/resolve-conflicts/SKILL.md`
- Each other skill or agent file that cites the old disagreement text (search for `needs-rework` and `disagreement`).

## Done means
- The files above state the new rule with the same words in each place.
- No file keeps the old text for these two labels.
- The PR body has the line `Process change: yes`. The PR does not edit `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION`.
- If an `xtask` test pins the old text, the test changes with it.

title: Windows: camcraft-ui lib test binary crashes (STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION) with 12 test threads; passes single-threaded

labels.name: P3

body:
### What happens

On two Windows 11 machines (bacon: Intel NUC with iGPU; lenny: desktop), the Windows quick check of `main` is red on one step:

```
FAIL  ui suites: lib  exit 101
process didn't exit successfully: `...\camcraft_ui-b30d80154151484e.exe --test-threads=12` (exit code: 0xc0000005, STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION)
```

The binary dies after about 100 tests with a native access violation, not a failed assert. Last tests printed before the crash (bacon, main `7a626a7f5`): the `egui_app::setup_plane_tests` / `setup_points_tests` group.

### It is a concurrency crash

The same binary, same tree, run single-threaded on bacon:

```
camcraft_ui-b30d80154151484e.exe --test-threads=1
test result: ok. 1425 passed; 0 failed; 7 ignored; finished in 166.04s
```

Linux (len, post-merge runners) and macOS (m3) are green on the same commits. Likely candidates: tests that create a graphics device/adapter (wgpu) or another thread-unsafe native resource in parallel. Related but different: #3258 (several UI binaries on one Linux host, fixed by #3302 naming the crash status); this one is one binary, several test threads, on Windows.

### Workaround

`--test-threads=1` for `camcraft-ui --lib` on Windows (the gate stays slower but green).

**Done means:** `cargo xtask gate quick` on Windows runs `ui suites: lib` green at its normal thread count, or the gate serialises exactly the tests that share the native resource, with a test or gate-plan pin and the crashing resource named in the decision note.

**Triage.** P3: a red gate on Windows only, with a workaround; no wrong output. `effort:medium`: test harness / gate plan, one crate.

labels.name: in-review

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

labels.name: P4
labels.description: Work the maintainer asked for, for the next cut

body:
The maintainer asked for this in chat on 2026-11-22, in his own words:

> issue; enhancement; support for tapered tooling like ball mills, roundover bits and similar, router style tooling.

Part of #3351. Refs #3351. This is sub-issue 1 of the plan in the research comments of #3351 (option C, the hybrid shape model).

## What to do

Add one internal shape type in `camcraft-tools`: the tool meridian. It is the cutting outline `rho(z)`, tip up, made of lines and circular arcs. All consumers read the tool shape through it in later sub-issues.

1. A new module (for example `crates/tools/src/meridian.rs`, under 400 lines). It holds the meridian type and `Tool::meridian()`. Reuse the point form of `SpunProfile` (`crates/tools/src/spun.rs`: `z`, `r`, signed `arc`).
2. `Tool::meridian()` gives the meridian of each existing mill kind from its numbers: `EndMill`, `BallNose`, `BullNose`, `Taper`, `Drill`, and the undercut heads of #1444 (`Lollipop`, `Dovetail`, `TSlot`, `Keyseat`). It agrees with `Tool::profile` (`crates/tools/src/tools.rs:387-465`) on the cutting band.
3. A split of the meridian into convex atoms:
   - a straight segment gives a frustum (each slope);
   - an arc that bulges away from the axis gives a torus zone;
   - an arc that bulges toward the axis gives chord frusta (outer bound) or tangent frusta (inner bound), with a sag limit as a parameter.
4. Each atom carries a flag: cutting, or non-cutting (a pilot bearing band).
5. Degenerate input (a zero-length segment, a negative radius, a non-finite value, an arc that does not fit its chord) gives a named error. It never panics.

No consumer changes in this issue. No toolpath, simulation or check changes.

## Rules

- The geometry is from elementary plane geometry (chord sag `R (1 - cos(theta / 2))`) and convexity (Boyd and Vandenberghe, Convex Optimization, 3.2.5). Each module has its provenance line. No HSMWorks material.
- `effort:max`: a new geometry algorithm and the shape law that the gouge checks will read.

## Done means

- `Tool::meridian()` exists for each mill kind listed above.
- Tests pin, for each existing kind, that its convex atoms are the same solids that `Cutter::atoms` (`crates/sim/src/verify/probe.rs:180-230`) builds today, within 1e-9 mm.
- Tests pin the outer and inner bounds of a concave arc: the outer union contains the arc, the inner union stays inside it, and each sag is under the limit.
- Tests pin a named error for each degenerate input.

The maintainer asked in chat on 2026-11-22 that the option "Pass starts at: Auto / Inside / Outside" go to every operation whose passes or rings have an order. The record of his words is on #3316. This issue is the part for **Bore**.

## What exists

PR #3353 (for #3316) adds the shared parameter for 2D Offset:
- The type `machining2d::PassStart { Auto, Inside, Outside }` and its ring law `PassStart::rank` (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/pass_start.rs`).
- One project key `pass_start` (`project::PassStartDto`). `auto` is never written.
- The generic MCP door `edit_operation`, and one Passes-tab row `Pass starts at` (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/pass_start_row.rs`).
- The design is in `docs/decisions/3316-pass-start-shared.md`.

## What to do

- Give Bore the field `pass_start` with the same type, key, row and MCP door. Do not make a new type.
- Make the planner of Bore read it. Where to look: the bore planner (the Bore kind in `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs`).
- Auto must keep the current output of Bore byte for byte (each golden).
- If Bore has no pass order, its row says so by name, and the issue records why.
- Leave room for the start point and the exit point of #1448 beside the parameter.

## Safety

The change can change posted moves. It is under the safety floor. The pin goes red first. The review is an independent read with a hand trace of one level.

Done means: Bore has the option in the property panel, in MCP and in the project file; Inside and Outside force the order; Auto keeps all shipped goldens byte-identical; a pin test shows the forced order.

The "Do not touch" group of the Geometry tab (Boundaries) does not work on a Engrave operation. The group shows only the note "'Do not touch' is supported on 2D Offset and 3D Pocket operations only so far". There is no "Pick protected" button. The maintainer asked for "do not touch" on operations, in his words: "the calculation should avoid to gouge them at all costs" (#2055).

Found during the work on #3335. Refs #2055. Refs #3335.

## What to do

1. Add `OpType::Engrave` to `do_not_touch_applies` (`crates/app/src/operation/types/avoid.rs`).

title: Start and exit points: move the picks to one operation-level project key

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Main is broken or a regression with no workaround; blocks a cut

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: area:3d
labels.description: 3D milling and finishing

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

body:
Refs #1448. Part of #1448. Follow-up of #3324.

## Why

The design of #3324 (`docs/decisions/1448-start-exit-shared.md`, section 2) chooses an operation-level project key for the start and exit picks. The PR of #3324 does not move the storage. The move puts one field on every path variant of `OpParams` and its DTO. More than ten open PRs change `wire_edm.rs` and `wire_edm_dto.rs`, so the move in the same PR conflicts with all of them.

The accessor `OpParams::path_picks()` hides the storage, so the family slices of #1448 that have a `links` field do not wait for this issue.

## What to do

- Store `camcraft_motion::path_picks::PathPicks` on every path kind.
- Write the key `picks: { start: [[x, y, z?], ...], exit: [...] }` at the operation level. Write it only when a list is not empty.
- Read the old keys on load: `links.approach.start_point`, `links.approach.exit_point` and the wire `start`.
- Keep the digest bytes `0xC7` / `0xC8` for the same values. No contour golden changes.
- Move `Approach::start_point` / `exit_point` and `WireContourOp.start` into the new field. Change `start_exit_rows.rs`, `start_exit_pick.rs` and the contour planner to read `path_picks()`.

## Done means

- A load test opens a file with the old `links.approach.start_point` key and a file with the old wire `start` key. The picks are the same after the load.
- Every contour golden and every contour pick test stays green with no change.
- This merges before the first family slice of #1448 for a kind with no `links` field (Face, turning, plasma).

title: Boundaries: one Boundary offset moves both the picked edge and the outer boundary - they need separate offsets

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: area:ui
labels.description: User interface and picking

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
The maintainer reported this in chat on 2026-11-22, in his own words:

> bug; boundaries; we should have control over how much the "outside boundary" offset is and the "inside boundary" offset is.. now its just boundary offset, which when i shrink it to a negative value also offsets the boundary from the face/edge i picked. Which makes it problematic to control the boundaries using the strategies choosen for example "Open-Machine side B". generates a very generous outside boundary that makes you cut air for a good halv a minute.

## What happens

The Boundary group has one row, "Boundary offset" (`AreaControls::offset`, `crates/app/src/operation/types/area.rs:86`; row in `crates/ui/src/egui_app/boundary.rs:114`). Its hint says: "+ grows the area outward, - shrinks it inward". The one value moves the whole area edge: the edge that the user picked (the face or the edge chain) and the outer boundary (the stock outline that an open boundary runs on to).

The user wants the outer boundary to be tighter. He sets a negative offset. The picked edge moves as well, so the area no longer starts at the face or edge that he picked. He cannot get both.

## The cost

With "Open - machine side B" the area is the part between the picked chain and the stock outline. The outer boundary is "very generous". The tool cuts air for about half a minute. The user has no way to shrink only that outer side.

## Expected

Two offsets, each with its own row and hint:

1. Offset of the picked edge or face (the inside boundary): moves the line that the user picked. Default 0.
2. Offset of the outer boundary (the outside boundary: the stock outline, or the open boundary's run-on): moves only that line. Default 0.

Each one applies to a closed boundary and an open boundary. A closed boundary that has only the picked loop uses the first one. The "Extend past open edges" value is separate, as it is now.

## Rules

- The default of both is 0 and the output is byte-identical for a project that has one `offset` value of 0. A project with a non-zero `offset` loads as the same value in BOTH new offsets: the output stays the same (project-file version bump and a migration test).
- The change is an undoable command (`EditOperationParams`). The MCP tool gets both fields.
- The region and the verify check read the same two values. The planner never refuses the picked line because the outer offset is negative.
- Safety floor: this changes the machined region. The pin goes red first, the review is an independent Opus read, and the heavy lanes that the diff reaches run.

## Done means

- A pin test: an open boundary, side B, on a model with a stock larger than the part. With the outer offset negative and the picked offset 0, the region edge on the picked chain stays on the chain, and the outer edge moves in. The cut-air length drops by the measured amount.
- A structural test of the two rows (labels, hints, default).
- The project-file migration test and a byte-identical golden for an old project.

title: Boundaries: "Do not touch" does not let the user pick a face or an edge

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:ui
labels.description: User interface and picking

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:medium
labels.description: One module or crate, a known pattern (issue-worker-medium)

labels.name: P3

body:
The maintainer reported this in chat on 2026-11-22, in his own words:

> Bug; the "do not touch" feature under boundaries, should allow me to pick a face or an edge. But i does not..

He did not say which operation kind he used, or what happens on a click. The worker finds this first.

## What the code says

The feature is #2055 (closed). The wanted behaviour: the "Do not touch" group of the Geometry tab lets the user click faces and edges in the viewport. Each pick shows as a row with a remove button.

Two readings of the report. The worker checks both:

1. The group is not usable for the operation kind that the maintainer uses. `do_not_touch_unsupported` (`crates/app/src/operation/types/avoid.rs:54`) says: "'Do not touch' is supported on 2D Offset and 3D Pocket operations only so far". For each other kind the group shows only that sentence. There is no "Pick protected" button (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/boundary.rs:305-314`). The wording "clear it on {kind}" does not say how to pick, and the group still shows in the Boundaries area where the user expects a pick control.
2. The group is usable (2D Offset, 3D Pocket), but the viewport click does not fill it. The click path is `take_pick` -> `take_do_not_touch_pick` (`crates/ui/src/boundary_draft.rs:355-398`). A click may go to the selection and not to the group, for example when a vertex is hit (the code ignores vertices), or when the group is in the "Picking…" state but another pick tool holds the viewport.

## Expected

- For each operation kind that has the group, a click on a face or an edge adds a row to "Do not touch". The status line says what was added.
- For a kind that does not support it, the user sees why, in plain words, and what to do. The better answer is to support the kind (the maintainer asked for "do not touch" on operations in #2055: "the calculation should avoid to gouge them at all costs").

## Done means

- A structural test in `crates/ui`: with the group open, a face click and an edge click each add one row; a remove click takes it away; the status line names the pick.
- The worker names the operation kind and the exact reason in a comment on this issue. If the cause is reading 1, the worker files one sub-issue per kind that lacks the feature (`Refs #2055`, bug, P3, source:agent, effort by the table; the safety floor applies to the generator work).
- The change goes through the same undoable command and MCP tool as the existing "Do not touch" picks.
