title: Start and exit points: the shared mechanism (design decision)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Main is broken or a regression with no workaround; blocks a cut

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: area:3d
labels.description: 3D milling and finishing

labels.name: area:ui
labels.description: User interface and picking

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server and agent tooling (crates/app/src/mcp, camcraft-mcp skill)

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

body:
Refs #1448. Part of #1448.

## Why

The maintainer set the scope of #1448 on 2026-11-22: a user-set start point and exit point on EVERY operation that cuts a path. He asked for one shared mechanism: one command, one MCP tool, one viewport pick, one pair of rows. He set it to `bug` and `P2`: "Mark them as P2 - they are bugs at this point".

Today only the closed 2D Contour rings take a start point and an exit point. The kind table is in the research comment on #1448. Each family sub-issue of #1448 depends on this issue.

The shared design is recorded in `docs/decisions/1448-start-exit-shared.md` before the next slice (comment on #1448, 2026-11-22).

## What `main` has

- `Approach::start_point` / `exit_point` (`crates/motion/src/approach.rs:162,168`): `Option<Point2>`, model XY in mm, inside `links.approach`.
- Kinds with a `links` field: Contour, Pocket, Adaptive2D, Offset2D, Circular, Slot, Pocket3D, RotaryOffset, MultiAxisRough, Bore. The other 33 path kinds have no `links`.
- The project keys `links.approach.start_point` / `exit_point` (`crates/app/src/project/approach.rs:77,81`). The digest bytes `0xC7` / `0xC8` (`crates/app/src/operation/params/digest.rs:202-212`).
- `EditOperationParams` (`crates/app/src/commands/operation/edit.rs`). `named_refusal` runs at create, edit and load (`sane.rs:54`).
- MCP: the generic patch of `edit_operation` (`crates/app/src/mcp/edit.rs:304-318`). The schema does not name the fields.
- UI: `start_exit_rows.rs` and `start_exit_pick.rs`, only on the 2D Contour lead tab (`approach_page.rs:140-182`).
- A second, separate start field: `WireContourOp.start` (`crates/app/src/operation/types/wire_edm.rs:61-63`).

## Open questions, options and the recommended option

### 1. One shared type

- A: Keep the fields in `links.approach`, and add `links` to each kind that has none.
- B: A new shared type in `camcraft-motion`, for example `PathPicks { start, exit }`. Every path kind holds it. One accessor `OpParams::path_picks()` reads it for every kind. The contour moves its two fields into it. Wire Contour moves `start` into it.
- C: A field for each kind.

Recommended: B. Option A gives `links` to kinds that have no links (turning, EDM, plasma), and the field has no meaning there. Option C repeats the refusal law 43 times.

Sub-question: the shape of a pick. Today it is a 2D point. A 3D finishing start, a multi-axis start and a turning (Z, X) start need more. Recommended: a pick holds a model-frame point with an optional Z. Each family projects it in its own frame (setup XY, the tilted frame, the lathe (Z, X) plane). Sub-question: one pick for each operation, or one for each chain or region (the #1448 body says "one pick per chain or region"). Recommended: the type holds a list from the first slice, so that the file format does not change again. A first slice can refuse a list longer than one by name.

### 2. The project key

- A: Keep `links.approach.start_point` / `exit_point`.
- B: A new key at the operation level (for example `picks: { start: [...], exit: [...] }`). The loader also reads the old `links.approach.*` keys and the old wire `start` key, so every saved file opens unchanged.

Recommended: B, with the old keys read on load. The digest keeps `0xC7` / `0xC8` for the same values, so a contour golden does not change.

### 3. The command

- A: `EditOperationParams`, as today.
- B: A dedicated `SetStartExit` command.

Recommended: A. One undo step can then change the pick and the "Pass starts at" option of #3316 together. The maintainer asked for one command.

### 4. The MCP tool

- A: The generic patch of `edit_operation`, as today, with the fields named in its schema.
- B: A dedicated tool, for example `set_start_exit`.

Recommended: A, with the fields named in the schema of `edit_operation` and a read-only answer (in the kind description) that says which kinds take a pick. Option B gives two doors to one command.

### 5. The viewport pick and the rows

- Recommended: one capability for each kind in `KindInfo` (`crates/app/src/operation/kinds.rs`), for example `Ring`, `Region`, `HoleOrder`, `Ends`, `Raster`, `NotTaken(reason)`.
- The pick snaps by capability: a wall for `Ring`, a point inside the region for `Region`, a hole for `HoleOrder`, an end for `Ends`, a corner for `Raster`.
- The rows of `start_exit_rows.rs` move to a shared group. Every operation page draws it.
- A kind with `NotTaken` draws the row with the reason by name (the maintainer: "Where a kind has no free start, the Start point row says so by name").

### 6. How the path is generated again to the point

- The pick is an input of the planner. The command changes the parameters. The normal generate runs after it, as for the contour today.
- Recommended: promote the ring helpers of `contour_start.rs` (`nearest_on_ring`, `reach`, `lead_held`) to a shared module in `crates/motion/src/`, for every ring and chain family.
- Each family keeps its own seam: re-sequence a ring, place the descent in a region, order the holes, choose an end, choose a raster corner.

### 7. Beside "Pass starts at" of #3316

- #3316 adds one shared parameter "Pass starts at: Auto / Inside / Outside" and its decision file `docs/decisions/3316-pass-start-shared.md`. This issue does not change it.
- The two choices work together. The pass side chooses which ring of a level cuts first. The start point chooses the place on that ring, and the descent place.
- Recommended order: the planner applies the pass side first, then projects the start pick onto the first ring that the pass side gives.
- A pick that the pass side makes impossible is refused by name. Example: "Outside" with a start pick inside the part.
- The design file names `3316-pass-start-shared.md` and keeps the two parameters as two fields in the same parameter group.

### 8. The refusal when a point cannot be reached

- A: Refuse by name (the contour law today).
- B: Move the pick to the nearest legal point and add a warning.

Recommended: A. The maintainer: "a pick is a wish. The planner refuses it by name when the lead law or the safety laws cannot hold it. It never moves the pick without a note."

Where each refusal runs:
- At command creation (`named_refusal`): the kind does not take a pick, the pick is not finite, or the pick is outside the setup.
- At generation: no lead fits, the helix does not fit, the pick is too far from the path, the pick conflicts with the pass side. The operation is refused, and the post is blocked.

Each message names the operation kind, the pick (start or exit), the reason and the user's next step.

## Done means

- `docs/decisions/1448-start-exit-shared.md` records each answer above: the choice, the reason and the dropped options.
- The shared type, the project key with the read of the old keys, the `edit_operation` schema fields, the `KindInfo` capability and the shared row group are on `main`.
- Every contour golden and every contour pick test stays green with no change.
- A load test opens a file with the old `links.approach.start_point` key and a file with the old wire `start` key.
- No family planner change is in this issue. The family sub-issues of #1448 do that.

> explpain these two errors.. travels.. should never be anywhere but at clearance plane.. so why does it do G0s below it?

and then: "file that as a P1 Bug."

## What happens

A 2D Offset operation generates rapid moves (G0) that run sideways below the clearance plane. They cross stock that is still uncut. The operation page shows this warning:

`rapid move 543 travels through stock (below the clearance plane, or at it below the stock top) - repeated on 2 more moves (to 1711)`

So three lateral rapids (move 543 up to move 1711) are below the clearance plane.

## Expected

"Hop below clearance" is off. The Heights tab says: "off, every link climbs to Clearance Z". Every lateral rapid then rides at the clearance plane (Z 32.000 here). No rapid runs sideways through stock.

## Evidence

- Build v0.25.0, commit 7e2a8119. The maintainer sent screenshots. They are not attached here.
- Operation `2D Offset1`: tool `EM-0800-4FL` (Ø8), model `fig8`, Setup1, VMC 3-AXIS, Siemens 840D. The Outside containment is the same as in #3316.
- Heights tab: Clearance Z = Top of stock +10 (Z 32.000). Top Z = Top of stock +0 (Z 22.000). Bottom Z = Selection +1.5 (Z 1.500). Stepdown 10 mm. "Hop below clearance" off.
- Lead in / Lead out tab: Level to level "Same as entry". Between levels "Clearance plane". Between passes "Retract plane". Plunge "Height above material" 2.0 mm. Entry Helix, radius 1.6 mm.
- Status: `OK - 1764 moves - 2 warnings`. The second warning is `move 522 cuts past the finish surface - repeated on 62 more moves (to 1710)`.

## What the code says (read by the coordinator on 2026-11-22)

- With the hop off, `retract_z` is `None`. Then `levels.rs:179` sets `hop_z = retract_z.unwrap_or(clearance_z).min(clearance_z)`. A link with the choice "Retract plane" lifts to the clearance plane (Z 32). There is no hidden retract plane (see #3318).
- So the three lateral rapids below Z 32 do not come from a pass link. Their source is not known. The worker finds it.

## Safety

The verifier flags these rapids and the post is blocked, so no wrong program is posted today. A rapid through stock is the failure that the verifier exists to stop. The generator must not make one. The priority is P1 on the word of the maintainer.

## Possible links

- #3316: the same operation. Its cause is the ring order: `waterscan.rs:115` sorts the rings core-first, so on an Outside band the first ring of each level is a full slot in the stock. The three rapids may be the jumps between rings that this order makes.
- #3318: the retract plane that the user cannot see. That answer is in this issue.
- #2121 (closed): a clearance plane set inside the stock. Not this case: here the clearance plane is above the stock top.

Done means: a pin test on `fig8.step` with `EM-0800-4FL` and these heights shows no lateral rapid below the clearance plane through stock, with "Hop below clearance" off; the verifier gives no `travels through stock` warning; every shipped golden is byte-identical; an independent Opus read and a hand trace of the three rapids.

The Lead in / Lead out tab of a 2D Offset operation has two link rows:
- "Between levels" is set to "Clearance plane".
- "Between passes" is set to "Retract plane".

The Heights tab has no Retract Z row. Its Levels group has only "Hop below clearance" (off) and "Stepdown". - The hint of the Heights tab says: "the retract plane: on, links hop at Retract Z; off, every link climbs to Clearance Z" (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/heights_page.rs`). The Retract Z row exists only while "Hop below clearance" is on.
- The Lead tab lists "Clearance plane / Retract plane / Keep down" for each link (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/lead_page.rs`). It does not say which height "Retract plane" means when the hop is off.
- The user guide says that a kind that has one gets a retract plane 10 above the stock top (`operations-2d.md`).

## Not known yet

Which height the generator uses for a link set to "Retract plane" when "Hop below clearance" is off, for 2D Offset. The hint of the Heights tab suggests the clearance height. The Lead tab suggests a separate plane. The worker reads the generator and says which one is true.

## Expected

One of these, and the maintainer chooses:
- "Retract plane" is shown on the Heights tab and in the viewport whenever a link uses it, with its value.

Its warning "rapid move 543 travels through stock (below the clearance plane, or at it below the stock top)" asks why three rapids are below the clearance plane. The answer may depend on this link. The worker of #3316 reads this issue.

title: 2D Offset with Outside containment: the passes start inside and cut from the inside out, so the tool slots in the stock

body:
The maintainer reported this in chat on 2026-11-22, in his own words:

> bug; Movement calcualtion; P2; Example 2D offset set with a outside continment, helixes dowwn inside of the calculated "containmen" and works its way from the inside out.. Which ends up being fully engagend slotting movements not following the rules where it should have been starting outside the part and worked itself in. We might need to add a option prob. undder "passes", that stats "Pass starts at <auto, inside, outside>".. where Auto is current behavior for setting it up and the other two forces either or. So we get control over the fact that it should not try to crate slots in the stock

## What happens

A 2D Offset operation has the containment "Outside". The tool helixes down inside the calculated containment. It then cuts the passes from the inside out. The result is fully engaged slotting moves in the stock.

## Expected

An "Outside" containment starts outside the part and works inward. The tool never makes a fully engaged slot in the stock.

## The change that the maintainer suggests

A new option on the Passes tab: "Pass starts at", with the values Auto, Inside and Outside.
- Auto keeps the current behaviour.
- Inside and Outside force the order.

The user then controls the order and stops the slots. This follows the rule that a strategy fork is an operation parameter with a default.

## Evidence

- Build v0.25.0, commit 7e2a8119 (built 2026-11-22 02:53 UTC). The maintainer sent a screenshot. It is not attached here.
- Operation `2D Offset1`: tool `EM-0800-4FL` (Ø8 end mill), model `fig8`, setup `Setup1`, machine VMC 3-AXIS, post Siemens 840D.
- The status line reads `OK - 8318 moves - 1 warning`. The warning reads: "feed moves 686 and 836 cross in XY at shared depth - repeated on 4 more moves (to 7496)". The operation tree shows 5 warnings.
- Lead in / Lead out tab: Entry type Helix, Helix radius 1.6 mm, Level to level "Same as entry", Between levels "Clearance plane", Between passes "Retract plane".
- The simulation at 60.7 / 1392.8 s shows the tool deep inside the machined area. The cut area around it is a closed slot.
- The maintainer's project file is a local file. Use the tracked model `testdata/models/fig8.step` and the tool `EM-0800-4FL` to reproduce.

## Possible link (not checked)

#2849, test 3 (`shoulder_adaptive::fig8_outside_containment_with_em0800_and_clearing_kinds_works`) uses the same model, the same tool and an "Outside" containment. Its body says that the last feed ends 31.406 mm from the part outline, and the PR #3267 says that a ring order change fixes it but turns `corner_arc_radius::the_crossing_law_keeps_the_arc_turns_and_crosses_nowhere` red. The two pins want opposite ring orders. A parameter for the order may settle both. The worker checks if this is the same defect and says so on both issues.

## Safety

A fully engaged slot overloads the tool. The toolpath is not a silent wrong cut, but it is a toolpath that the user must not run. If the fix changes pass order or the posted moves, it is under the safety floor: the pin goes red first, and the review is an independent Opus read with a hand trace.

Done means: a pin test shows an Outside containment that starts outside and cuts inward on `fig8.step` with `EM-0800-4FL`, with no move whose engagement is a full slot; the new option and its three values are in the property panel and in MCP; Auto keeps the current output of all shipped goldens.

body:
Research only: no code, no branch, no PR, no lane slot (AGENTS.md "needs-research is research, not code").

## Why
CamCraft ships 48 machine files (`assets/machines/*.mch`), but the simulation shows each machine as simple blocks and cylinders (#2584). Many machine makers publish real 3D models of their machines, so the posed machine could look like the actual machine.

## Questions to answer (in comments on this issue)
1. **Which machines have a public 3D model?** For each `.mch` file, list: the maker's page, the format (STEP, Parasolid, IGES, STL...), whether the model is split into moving parts (table, saddle, head, spindle, rotary axes) or is one solid, its size, and the **licence or terms of use**.
   Machines: 3axis-vmc, agiecut-classic-2s, doosan-dnm(-3axis), fehlmann-picomax55, grbl-3axis, grblhal-3axis, haas-dm1, haas-dt1, haas-mini-mill, haas-vf2, haas-vf2ss, lathe, linuxcnc-3axis, makera-carvera(-air), makera-z1, millturn, sienci-altmill-2x4/4x4/4x8, sinker-edm, sodick-alc400g, tilthead, tinyg-3axis, the Tormach range (440, 770/770M/770M+/770MX/-ML/microarc4, 1100 S1-S3/M/M+/MX, 1300PL, 1500MX, 8L, 15L/15LX Slant-Pro, 24R, xsTECH/Pro), vmc. Generic files (vmc, 3axis-vmc, lathe, millturn, tilthead, the grbl/tinyg/linuxcnc ones) need no vendor model; say so.
2. **Download** each model that may be downloaded for local use into `~/m5data/machine-cad/<machine>/` on M5, with a `SOURCE.md` per machine: the URL, the date, the licence text or a link to it, and the file's sha256. **Never commit them to this repo or rehost them anywhere** unless the licence clearly allows redistribution. Do not download anything behind a login or sign-up form; list it as "needs a human" instead.
3. **Can CamCraft show them?** Check each model against what the sim view needs:
   - Can its parts be mapped to the `.mch` axis tree (which part moves with X, Y, Z, A, B, C)?
   - How many triangles does each part have after meshing at display resolution? Is decimation needed?
   - Where is its origin compared with the `.mch` machine zero?
4. **Where it should live.** Pick one, with the reasons:
   - (a) in CamCraft: a STEP or mesh body per part in the `.mch` file (#2591), loaded from a path the user supplies, since the model itself is not ours to ship;
   - (b) a side project: a fetch script plus per-machine part maps in `mkinney/cam-tools-and-fixtures` (the same pattern as its vendor fixture fetch), which CamCraft reads when present;
   - (c) URDF assemblies (#2593), for example built in SolidCraft from the vendor STEP.

## Clean-room limits
Use machine makers' own public downloads only. **No models from Autodesk, Fusion, HSMWorks or any other CAM vendor's machine library**, and nothing taken from another CAM product's install.

## Done means
- One comment per machine family with the table from question 1.
- The models that may be downloaded are in `~/m5data/machine-cad/`, each with its `SOURCE.md`.
- A recorded decision on (a), (b) or (c).
- The concrete sub-issues for that decision are filed, each with one `P*`, one `effort:*`, `area:*`, `source:agent`, "Part of #this" and a "Done means" line. This issue is then closed.

Related: #2584 (simple machine model), #2591 (STEP body in .mch), #2593 (machine from URDF), #2587 (sim view).

Rotary Offset with strategy Zigzag or Auto plans each developed level with `machining3d::hsm::plan_level`, with a seam. The level gets Zigzag rows only. A row touches a shoulder wall or an island only at its ends. A cusp can stay between each two ends, as in #3129.

PR #3167 adds closing rings to the 3D pocket levels. It does not add them to the wrap levels (`seam.is_some()`). The developed area of a wrap level ends at the seam. A ring on each boundary loop also follows the two seam edges of the strip. These two edges are one physical line, so the ring cuts that line two times.

## Expected
The Zigzag rows of a wrap level close with a ring on each wall and island. The ring does not follow the seam edges of the developed strip.

## Notes
- `crates/app/tests/rotary_verify.rs::a_rough_over_an_oversized_bar_peels_from_the_stock_radius` pins the move count of the matching bar (2064). A full ring on the developed area gave 2863 moves.
- First, measure the shoulder cusp on a wrap level with rows only. If there is no cusp, close this issue with the reading.

## Done means
A pin measures the shoulder or island wall of a Rotary Offset Zigzag level. It fails before the change and passes after it. The crossing check and the rotary verify stay clean.

body:
## What are you trying to do

Post a rectangular wire EDM punch to an Agie Classic Cut 2S from the desktop or a command script. The controller needs a linked ISO contour, SBR resource list and SBL job. The generic ISO wire post writes a single program.

## How you imagine it working

Select the native post and a compatible machine. Select the controller separation length explicitly. Write all three files to a new job directory. Refuse an unsupported setup without creating output. The controller applies its resident wire compensation to the nominal contour.

The proposed first case is one vertical rectangular punch in 20 mm stock, with a 0.25 mm wire and a 1 mm separation cut. An offline control accepted a synthetic 40 by 20 mm example. Its graphical check showed a rough pass, three trims and a final separation sequence. This was a software check. A physical machine was not tested.

## Source decision

The proposed writer draws on an independently developed MIT-licensed implementation. Its source notes attribute some interface details to observations of controller examples. The native job uses a resident technology selection. We have not verified a public programming manual for all required call arguments and selection values. No vendor runtime, control image or technology table is proposed for distribution.

Does this reference meet the project's clean-room source rules for an EDM post? If a different reference is required, which published programming reference should we use?

Done means: The project accepts the sources for the post. The desktop and command script produce the same complete native job. Tests pin the supported output, refuse unsupported setups, and preserve an existing destination.

1. **Unmeasured face.** `Unmeasured::NoSurface` (`crates/kernel/src/mesh_deviation.rs`, mapped to `MeshRefusal::Unmeasured` in `machining_mesh.rs`) is never forced by a test. Old pins: `step_fit_tests.rs` (`a_face_without_surface_parameters_is_logged_and_reported_unmeasured` and its twin).
2. **Boundary point on its own sheet.** No test puts a boundary point of a many-turn flank, a root band or a fold through the reader and asserts its sheet or a refusal. Only `twisted_flank.step` (volume) and `twisted_flank_off.step` (refusal) pin the class. Old pins: `step_nearest_tests.rs` (8).
3. **Orientation in every order.** No test asserts that the outward result is the same when the facets or faces come in another order. Old pins: `step_orient_tests.rs` (`conflicting_votes_give_one_answer_on_every_run_and_in_every_order`, `the_first_gap_named_is_the_same_in_every_order`).
4. **Seam bow against the gap tolerance.** No STEP-level test asserts that a seam bowed within the tolerance closes and a seam past it is refused. Old pins: `step_seams_tests.rs` (`a_boundary_bowed_within_the_gap_tolerance_is_closed`, `the_importer_closes_seams_within_two_chord_tolerances_only`).

No wrong output is known. The solidcore internals are in the external `solidcore` git dependency, so each pin is a fixture or a record edit at the kernel seam (`crates/kernel/tests/`).

Done means: each of the four laws has a pin in `crates/kernel/tests/` (or `crates/geometry/tests/`), or the decision file records why the law has no object for solidcore, with the reading that proves it.

title: 3D Finish: an option to stop the waterline ring pass on steep flanks

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:3d
labels.description: 3D milling and finishing

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P6
labels.description: Accepted enhancement, not scheduled

body:
## What is asked

A contributor asks for one control on 3D Finish: a switch that turns off the waterline ring pass, so the operation cuts its raster lines only. The contributor's words, quoted unchanged (chat, 2026-11-19):

> how hard would it be to make a checkbox that can disable the waterline portion?

## What the tool does today

A Parallel 3D Finish operation splits the terrain at 45 degrees. Shallow facets get the Z-following raster lines. Steep facets get waterline rings: `parallel()` runs one raster pass, then `rings_and_tail` (`crates/motion/src/finishing3d/raster.rs` line 210). The ring paths run about 90 degrees across the raster lines. Every wall that stands above the Bottom plane gets its ring ladder: hole walls, end walls, and the sloped edges of a tilted top face.

The picture below shows a contributor's test part: a long bar with a top face tilted 2 degrees and two openings, cut with a 0.3125 in ball-end, Bottom 0.300 in. The purple arrow marks one ring run that still survives on a wall near the near end. The tall ladders at the far end wall are the same law at the high end of the sloped face. The raster family cannot cover those walls; only the rings can.

![Ring run surviving on a wall at Bottom 0.300 in, parallel to the bar length and near the near end edge](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FlamingFireCoding/Camcraft/screenshots/issue-2811-waterline-arrow.png)

## Why the switch is wanted

On a part whose steep flanks are out of scope, the rings add cutting time, and they add paths the machinist did not ask for. Some machinists want the lines only, and accept the walls as they stand. One checkbox should say that choice out loud.

## Proposed shape

- One parameter, for example `waterlines: bool`, default on. Existing behaviour does not change.
- GUI name: not just "off". The control must name the consequence, for example "Steep flanks: Waterlines / Leave uncut".
- The switch applies to the Parallel pattern. Whether Parallel multi and Scallop take it is a decision. Blend should likely never take it: its 30-45 degree double cut needs the rings to remove the staircase (its own note says so). The maintainer decides this scope.

## Laws the switch must keep

1. With the switch off and steep flanks present, the path must carry a visible note that names the uncut flanks and their count. Silent rest material is not allowed (Prime Directive).
2. A model that is fully steep with the switch off must refuse with a clear error, not post an empty program. The raster answers `false` for an all-steep model; today "the rings alone carry it".
3. The parameter round-trips in the project file. Old project files load with the default, on.
4. The 3D finish MCP parameter surface exposes the same field (same rule as `fill_openings` and `gap_link`).

## Measured support (headless probe, main `744c0847b`)

Synthetic model: bar 24 x 160 mm, flat bottom z 0, top face sloped 2 degrees, two through openings, ball 7.94 mm, Parallel, gap link Jump. The probe classifies the XY direction of every Feed move.

- Bottom 0: 188 along-wall Y-family Feed runs at Z ladder levels about 0.4 mm apart. Zero Feed runs cross the open top face. All perpendicular feed sits on walls.
- Bottom raised to 9.75 mm (near the high top edge): the same perpendicular runs collapse to three ladder levels per wall, and only over the stretch where the face still stands above Bottom. Nothing sits in the open middle.

This matches the picture: raising Bottom shrank the ring set everywhere except where walls still rise above it. The behaviour is correct as designed; this issue asks for control, not for a defect fix. The probe code can become the pinning test for the switch.

## Done means

- A checkbox flips the ring pass on and off, and each state has a motion test that pins it.
- Off plus steep flanks: a note names the uncut flanks; no ring moves appear in the CL output.
- Off plus a steep-only model: a refusal with a clear message.
- Project-file round-trip test and MCP parity pass.
- The 3D finish page shows the control with its consequence wording.

## Classification

This account is a contributor and cannot set labels. Suggested labels, for a maintainer: `enhancement`, `P6`, `effort:high` (safety floor: it changes posted G-code when the switch is used), `area:motion`, `area:ui`, `area:mcp`. The body was written by the contributor's agent at the contributor's request.

body:
Requested by flamingfire (Discord, relayed by the user, 2026-11-19), while setting up the helical rotor of #2772 on an A table.

## What happens

The rotary operations (Rotary Contour, Rotary Parallel, Rotary Offset) show the same Heights page as the 3-axis operations: Clearance, Retract, Top and Bottom as Z values in the setup frame (the viewport labels them, e.g. "Clearance 3.6733 (stock top +0.9843)"). On a part that turns about A, a Z plane is the wrong shape: the tool must keep its distance from the axis all the way round. The #1904 walkthrough already notes that "Bottom Z is a floor in the laid frame, not a radius".

## Wanted

For an operation on a rotary, the heights are cylinders about the fitted (or, after #2772, stated) rotary axis:

- **Clearance radius** and **retract radius**: the tool moves between cuts at this distance from the axis while A turns;
- **Top radius** / **bottom radius** (or depth from the stock skin): the radial band the passes cut, the 4-axis equivalent of Top/Bottom;
- each one offered "from stock OD", "from model max radius" or an absolute radius, the way the Z heights offer "from stock top / model top" today;
- the viewport draws them as cylinders (or circles in the axis view), not planes.

## Safety

- Every radius is checked against the stock and the fixture (chuck, tailstock): a clearance radius inside the stock's largest radius is refused at the setting, not found at simulation.
- The A-only moves (the part turns while the tool waits) happen at the clearance radius, so they are judged by the existing swing / collision checks.
- Changes the posted G-code of rotary operations: golden tests for the old Z-height behaviour stay until the new heights are the default, and the change is noted as breaking for rotary projects if the saved fields change.

## Done means

A rotary operation shows the four heights as radii, the generated path keeps them (pinned by a test that measures the tool tip's distance from the axis on every link and rapid), the viewport draws them about the axis, and a radius inside the stock is refused by name.

Related: #2772 (stated axis for a helical part).

body:
Follow-up of PR #2717 (review 5974923122, a note that was not a blocker).

## What is wrong

`RasterGrid::cell_rect` in `crates/geometry/src/nesting/raster.rs` multiplies two `i64` values (`i * cell`) before the add. `RasterGrid::new` proves only that `origin + n * cell` fits in `i64`. With an origin near `i64::MIN` and a cell near `i64::MAX / n`, the intermediate product can overflow.

No current path can build such a grid: `covering` keeps the origin near the region. The code has no callers outside its tests. Thus this is owed hardening, not a defect.

## What to do

- Compute the corner in `i128` and convert to `i64` with a checked conversion.
- Refuse an overflow by name. Do not wrap and do not panic.
- Add one test with a hand-made grid at the limits.

Done means: `cell_rect` has no unchecked `i64` product, and the test pins the limit case.

title: Research: dynamic test impact analysis for post-merge gates - coverage map + failure history to run likely failures first

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:build
labels.description: Build, CI, release, tests

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

labels.name: P8
labels.description: Larger idea needing design or research before code

body:
**Research only** (AGENTS.md "needs-research"): answer the questions, then file concrete sub-issues.

## Why
A post-merge gate should **fail fast**: the tests most likely to break after a merge should run first, so a red main is known in minutes, not after ~54 min. Today the order is fixed, and the only change-aware selection is the quick tier's hand-written gate maps (`Gate map (M4.4): covers ...`).

Motivating case (2026-11-19): PR #2664 changed the STEP importer and turned two suites red that its gate maps did not name: `camcraft-app feature_edge_g1_join` and `camcraft-kernel step_agreement` (#2713). Both were found only by the full post-merge run.

## Idea (dynamic, from the code and history - not hand maps)
1. **Coverage map:** after each green full run (or nightly), run the suites under coverage (`cargo llvm-cov`, per test) and store a map: test -> files/functions it executed. On a merge, the tests that executed the changed lines run first. (Here: `step_agreement` executes the STEP importer, so it would have ranked first.)
2. **Failure history:** record, per gate run, which tests failed and which files changed. Rank tests by P(fail | changed files) / duration; boost recent failures and new tests.
3. **Graph fallback:** the repo's graphify graph (`graphify affected`) for test -> code wiring when no coverage data exists for a file.
4. **Execution:** feed the ranked list to a parallel runner (nextest or the release-queue lanes, #2727), which starts each test as soon as its binary is built. The FULL suite still runs; ranking only changes the ORDER (the map can be wrong; a skip must never hide a failure).

## Open questions
1. Cost and stability of a per-test coverage run for the whole workspace (time on a 16-32 vCPU box; size of the map; how often to refresh it).
2. Granularity: file, function or line; how renames and moved code keep their history.
3. How the ranking reaches the gate (an input file to `xtask`, or a nextest filter/order).
4. Where the history lives (a file in the repo, a gate artifact, the post-merge workflow's cache).
5. Measured value: replay recent red post-merge runs and report time-to-first-failure with and without ranking.

title: Gouge check: GPU segment-facet pair filter before the exact f64 facet gouge law

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:sim
labels.description: Stock simulation and verification

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

labels.name: P4
labels.description: Work the maintainer asked for, for the next cut

body:
Part of #2526 (GPU shader toolpath generation). Slice 4 of 5. Needs #2620 (compute seam).

Maintainer order (2026-11-18): "GPU shader issues get priority". Thus this issue is `P4`.

## Why
The facet gouge law measures the exact distance between each ball-center segment and each model triangle (`crates/sim/src/stock_sim/gouge.rs`: `facet_gouge` lines 43-172, `dist_seg_tri` line 174). Facets are already put in XY bins (lines 65-131). On a very long program against a very large mesh the pair count is still high.

## What
- A compute kernel marks the (segment, bin) pairs whose conservative distance is below `r + margin`. f32, tile-relative coordinates, margin larger than the stated f32 error bound.
- The CPU measures every marked pair with the f64 `dist_seg_tri`. The gouge depth and its location stay the f64 values.
- The kernel only removes pairs. It never adds a gouge, and it never sets a depth.
- With no GPU, or with the GPU off, `facet_gouge` runs as today.

## Prime Directive
- A gouge must block the post. An unmarked pair that has a gouge is the one risk. Thus the filter is a superset test, and it has a CPU parity test.
- Fault injection test: a kernel margin set to a negative value must make the parity test fail. The test proves that the parity test can catch a miss.

## Pinning tests (CPU reference)
- For the gouge fixtures of the sim suites, the GPU-marked pair set is a superset of the CPU pairs with distance below `r`.
- The gouge verdicts (depth, location, refusal text) are the same with the GPU on and off.
- Skip and fail policy of `headless_gpu` (#615, `CAMCRAFT_REQUIRE_GPU=1`).

## Decision entry
Yes, if `camcraft-sim` gets an edge onto the compute crate of #2620. Recommended instead: the app computes the pair mask and passes it to `facet_gouge` as a value, so `camcraft-sim` stays GPU-free.

Effort: `effort:max` (gouge check; safety floor).

Done means: the GPU pair filter feeds `facet_gouge`, the verdicts are equal with the GPU on and off, the superset and fault injection tests pass, and the PR states the time readings on a long program.

title: 3D finishing: GPU inverse-offset height bound as a first filter for the f64 drop-cutter

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:3d
labels.description: 3D milling and finishing

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

body:
Part of #2526 (GPU shader toolpath generation). Slice 3 of 5. Needs #2619 (CPU facet grid) and #2620 (compute seam).

Maintainer order (2026-11-18): "GPU shader issues get priority". Thus this issue is `P4`.

## What
- A compute kernel computes, for each cell of a tile, a conservative bound of the ball support height: the inverse tool offset of the facets on a grid (M. Inui, "Fast inverse offset computation using polygon rendering hardware", Computer-Aided Design 35(2), 2003; the Z-map model of B. K. Choi and R. B. Jerard, "Sculptured Surface Machining", 1998).
- f32, tile-relative coordinates. The margin is larger than the stated f32 error bound of the kernel (WGSL "Floating Point Accuracy": division 2.5 ULP, `inverseSqrt` 2 ULP). The PR states the bound and how the margin covers it.
- The CPU uses the bound only to skip facets in `support_at` (`crates/motion/src/finishing3d/support.rs` 368-388) that cannot be the highest support.
- The posted height stays the f64 `support_at` value at the true sample point. `ball_clear` (lines 132-142) stays the certifier, in f64, against every facet of the CPU grid near the ball. The GPU never removes a facet from `ball_clear`.
- The app makes the GPU result in the generate job (`crates/app/src/commands/operation/generate.rs`), once for each operation, and passes it to motion as a value. Never in a frame. The CLI and MCP use the same path.
- With no GPU, or with the GPU off, motion runs the #2619 CPU path. The result is the same bytes.

## Prime Directive
- A wrong bound can only skip the true support. Then `ball_clear` refuses the lower candidate, and the march searches higher or refuses by name. A GPU error cannot make a gouge pass. A test pins this with a deliberately wrong bound (a fault injection test).
- The tolerance is not tied to the grid resolution. The grid only filters.

## Pinning tests (CPU reference)
- GPU on and GPU off give the same `.cl` and `.cnc` bytes on the 3D finishing goldens of `crates/app/tests/golden/`. Run on the software adapter; on hardware where present.
- The fault injection test above: a bound raised by a large value gives a refusal or the same output, never a lower cutter.
- Skip and fail policy of `headless_gpu` (#615, `CAMCRAFT_REQUIRE_GPU=1`).

## Readings
Time of one large 3D finishing operation: CPU grid only (#2619) against CPU grid plus GPU filter, release build, with upload and readback times. If the GPU does not gain on the large fixtures, the PR says so and the switch stays off by default.

## Decision entry
Only if a new crate edge is added past the ones of #2620.

Effort: `effort:max` (toolpath geometry algorithm on a new compute path; safety floor).

Done means: the GPU bound filters the support scan, the goldens are byte-equal with the GPU on and off, the fault injection test passes, and the PR states the readings.

title: GPU compute seam: a headless compute crate with capability probe, CPU fallback and one parity-tested kernel (facet binning)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:3d

body:
Part of #2526 (GPU shader toolpath generation). Slice 2 of 5. Needs slice 1 (#2619) for the CPU reference.

Maintainer order (2026-11-18): "GPU shader issues get priority". Thus this issue is `P4`.

## Why
Only `camcraft-ui` links wgpu today, through the `egui_wgpu::wgpu` re-export (`Cargo.toml` lines 46-47). The generators run in `camcraft-app` and `camcraft-motion`, and in the CLI and MCP with no window. They have no GPU access. The headless device policy exists, but in `crates/ui/src/headless_gpu.rs`.

## What
- A new crate (recommended name `camcraft-gpu`) for headless compute. It holds:
  - The device policy of `headless_gpu.rs` (software adapter first in tests, then hardware), moved down from `camcraft-ui`. `camcraft-ui` then uses it.
  - A capability probe: `DownlevelFlags::COMPUTE_SHADERS`, `max_storage_buffer_binding_size`, `max_compute_workgroup_storage_size`. WebGL2 and GL below ES 3.1 have no compute: the probe says "no compute" by name.
  - One device for each process, made on the first request and cached (`OnceLock`). Never made for each operation or each frame.
  - A switch to turn the GPU off (recommended: `CAMCRAFT_GPU_COMPUTE=off`) for tests and for machines with bad drivers (#2424, #74).
  - One kernel: conservative facet binning. Input: facet boxes in tile-relative f32, padded by `r` plus a margin. Output: the cell lists.
- The CPU path runs, with the same result, when there is no adapter, the probe fails, the device is lost, or a buffer is past the limit. The log names the reason one time. Never a panic, never `unwrap` on a GPU future.

## Pinning tests (CPU reference)
- Superset parity: for the same facets, each facet in the CPU grid cell of #2619 is in the GPU cell list. Extra GPU entries are permitted.
- Refusals: a buffer past the limit, and a forced "no compute" probe, give `Err` with the reason. The caller uses the CPU grid.
- Adapter policy: the `headless_gpu` rule (#615). No adapter prints a loud SKIP. `CAMCRAFT_REQUIRE_GPU=1` turns the skip into a failure. The self-hosted runners have the Mesa software drivers (`runners` skill), so the lane runs on lavapipe there.

## Decision entry and dependencies
- A `docs/decisions/` entry is necessary: new crate edges (`camcraft-ui` and `camcraft-app` onto the new crate). The entry lists the imported items and what rebuilds.
- A direct `wgpu` dependency is new for the workspace. The version must be the one that the egui set pins (`=30.0.1` with egui-wgpu `=0.36.2`), so no second wgpu enters the lock. The review sets `needs-maintainer` for this dependency, by AGENTS.md.
- The wgpu version then moves with the egui set (#658, #1118). The decision entry says so.
- `camcraft-motion` gets no GPU dependency. The app computes the GPU result and passes it into motion as a value.

Effort: `effort:high` (several crates, new behaviour with its tests). No posted output changes in this slice.

Done means: the new crate exists with the probe, the cached device, the CPU fallback and the binning kernel; the superset parity test passes on the software adapter; `camcraft-ui` uses the moved device policy; the decision entry is in the PR.

1. **Rigid tapping:** the post writes `G84 ... F` with no `M29`. On a 31i, G84 is rigid without M29 only when parameter 5200 bit 0 is set. Does this machine need `M29 S..` before G84? If so: a post option (or the default) that writes `M29 S..`.
2. **Peck cycle:** the post writes `G73` (chip break) for a peck drill, at `R0.` (the part top) after a rapid to Z0. Is G73 the right default, or G83 (full retract)? Should R be 1-2 mm above the top?
3. **G05.1 Q1 R1:** the post does not write it today (#616: G5.1 states no tolerance, so it only names the smoothing request in a comment). Where does the owner put `G05.1 Q1 R1` / `G05.1 Q0` (after the tool change, per operation)? That decides a post option.

## Test kit (graph check only - test tools and holes, do not cut)

Tool numbers are test numbers, T12 face mill, T13 D6 end mill, T14 D6 drill, T15 M6 tap - chosen to stay off T1, the owner's probe ("I will not face with my probe!"). Change them to your own pockets first. Each program's first comment says so.

Posted 2026-11-18 by CamCraft main (v0.24.0 code), built-in Fanuc post, generic 3-axis VMC, metric, part = a 120 x 80 x 12 mm aluminium bracket, G54 = top front-left of the stock.

- `01-two-tools.nc`: face with T12 (D10), outside contour 2 mm deep with T13 (D6): tool change, `G43 H`, G2/G3 arcs.
- `02-peck-drill.nc`: seven holes, D6 drill, peck 3 mm (`G73`).
- `03-rigid-tap.nc`: M6 x 1.0 tap on the same holes (`G84`, no `M29`).

body:
Part of #2574 (research answer 1, options b and c).

Maintainer request, 2026-11-18, in his words (quoted in #2574):
> "This could be refined further in the mch file with its own definition language or even point at source .step file to be the "parts"."

## Recommended in #2574
One optional key `body` on a part, in three layers:
- No `body`: the generated body (#2584).
- `"body": { "primitives": [ { "box": ... }, { "cylinder": ... }, { "cone": ... } ] }`: primitives in the part frame. This is JSON in the existing grammar, not a second language (a second parser was dropped).
- `"body": { "step": "<path relative to the .mch>" }`: one STEP file, read with the solidcore STEP reader through `camcraft-geometry`.

## Scope
- Grammar and reader in `camcraft-post::machine` (`MachineTree`, #2583), documented in `assets/machines/AGENTS.md`. A bad value refuses the file by the part id and the key.
- The machine model (#2584) builds the stated body in place of the generated one.
- A missing or unreadable STEP file refuses that body by name. The machine-part check reports "not judged" for it. It never falls back to a generated body without a note.
- A body from a file is not marked "generated".
- The Machines pane validator (`crates/app/src/machine/validate.rs`) refuses the same values.
- Degenerate STEP input gives a clean error (fuzz with the existing importer fixtures).

## Done means
Tests pin the parse of each layer, the refusals by name, the STEP load of one part, and the "not judged" line for a missing STEP file.

Depends on #2583 and #2584.

body:
Proposal from mkinney (2026-11-18): "Should we formalize our QA swarm in an issue ... so all can track what it is doing? ... It is starting to feel like integration tests."

What exists: since 2026-11-17 mkinney's agents design parts in the latest SolidCraft and make them in the latest CamCraft end to end (design -> project -> operations -> generate -> verify -> post), and write a report per part. Ten parts so far (p01-p10: flange, bracket, stepped block, threaded boss, wrapped cylinder, all-ops mill part, lathe shaft, microARC 4 part, turning on a mill, plasma plate). They found about 100 problems; filed so far: #2437, #2440, #2443, #2578, #2579, #2580.

## Proposal: two layers

1. **Deterministic (in the normal gate, no AI):** every QA part that posts becomes an example-catalog case (#2392, `cargo xtask catalog`): the `.sc`/`.step`, a recorded build script (the MCP/CamScript steps) and the byte-pinned `.nc`. A regression then shows in the normal gate at no AI cost.
2. **Exploratory (agents, on contributors' own machines, NOT in GitHub Actions):** the agents need AI subscriptions and keys, and AGENTS.md keeps secrets off the self-hosted runners. Runs are made visible by:
   - one pinned tracking issue with a comment per run (versions, parts, results, issues filed);
   - the part briefs in the repository (for example `qa/briefs/`), so anyone can read and improve them;
   - a `source:qa` label on every issue a run files.

## When to run

- after each minor cut tag (test what users download);
- after each SolidCraft release, at most daily (the `.sc` import, #2578, broke this way);
- on demand.

## Decisions for the maintainer

- Do passing parts go into the catalog (#2392) as cases, and is the repository the right home for the briefs?
- The `source:qa` label.

title: Research: turning on a mill (part in the spindle, lathe tools on the table, one WCS per tool), e.g. Tormach RapidTurn on a 770MX

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:turning
labels.description: Lathe and mill-turn

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: needs-research
labels.description: Large idea with open questions: research and file sub-issues before any code

labels.name: effort:max

labels.name: P8
labels.description: Larger idea needing design or research before code

body:
Asked by mkinney (2026-11-18), who has a Tormach 770MX: "you can use a 3d mill like a lathe ... You end up using multiple WCS for each tool and put part in spindle". Wording: this is **turning on a mill (part in spindle)**, not live tooling on a lathe (CamCraft's existing "Mill-turn" machine).

## The setup

- The workpiece is held in a collet in the mill spindle and turns (M3/M4 at lathe speeds).
- Lathe tools (turning, facing, grooving, threading, parting) are clamped on the table in a gang row.
- There is no tool change: each tool is selected by switching to its own work offset (G54...G59, G59.1-3, G54.1 Pn) whose origin is that tool's tip relative to the spindle centre line.
- One length offset describes the part in the spindle: collet nose to the end of the stock stick-out (`G43 H<n>` once; the user keeps T255 for it).
- Lathe Z (along the part) is the mill Z; lathe X (diameter) is a table axis toward the spindle centre line.

## What CamCraft does today (QA run p09, main `83867fd7`)

- No way to declare "part in spindle, tools on the table".
- A lathe operation set accepted on a 3-axis mill machine posts lathe code labelled "Tormach 770MX" with no warning (high; filed separately).

## Open questions

1. Machine description: a part-in-spindle mode, tool stations on the table (position, side of the spindle, WCS), the collet nose and the stock stick-out.
2. Operations: reuse the turning operations; what changes in the X sign and spindle direction per side; constant surface speed vs fixed RPM on a mill spindle; feed per rev.
3. Post: a WCS switch per tool, no M6, safe retracts between stations, the one `G43 H` for the stock.
4. Safety checks: tool blocks vs the collet and the part, max spindle RPM with a part in it, chip direction.
5. Sources: Tormach's public RapidTurn documentation (operator manual UM10393, D32901, TD10561); the user's own 770MX tests.

Plan (user): several CamCraft simulations first, then PathPilot Hub, then air cuts, then real cuts - slowly.

labels.name: enhancement

labels.name: area:post

labels.description: Fix pushed on a branch with an open PR; merges at the next cut

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P6
labels.description: Accepted enhancement, not scheduled

body:
## Request

A built-in post for Hurco mills with the WinMax control, writing **NC/ISO programs** (Hurco's ISNC dialect, the Fanuc-like one), plus a machine file for a typical 3-axis Hurco VMC. Conversational (Hurco's own format) is out of scope.

A machine owner in the community runs a Hurco with **WinMax 09.01.393.30 (May 2019)**, NC/ISO programs only. WinMax simulates the full toolpath on the machine's screen, so each program can be checked at the control before it cuts, like the PathPilot Hub checks for Tormach.

## Clean-room sources (only these)

- Hurco's public WinMax help: the NC programming G-code table (it marks which codes are ISNC, BNC or both), NC M codes, NC part programming principles, NC parameters (support.hurco.com, WinMax Mill help, NC_Programming section).
- Hurco's public WinMax Mill documentation PDF (704-0116-101).
- What the owner's WinMax simulator accepts and shows.
- Never another CAM product's Hurco post or its output.

## What to decide from the docs

- Program start and end words, program number/comment format, units (G20/G21), the safe start line.
- Tool change (`T.. M6`) and length offset (`G43 H..`); does WinMax want a separate tool-length table call.
- Canned cycles available in ISNC (G73, G81-G89 with G98/G99) and their word formats (Q, P dwell units).
- Arcs (I/J/K vs R), work offsets (G54-G59 and the extended set), coolant, spindle words.
- Anything ISNC requires that Fanuc does not, or refuses that Fanuc allows.

## Done means

- A built-in post `Hurco WinMax (NC)` and a machine file.
- Goldens for contour, pocket, drill, peck, tap, two tools, two work offsets; a test that no word outside the documented ISNC set is written.
- One short program per question checked in the owner's WinMax simulator (load without error, the sim path matches CamCraft's), recorded on this issue.

body:
Found while the v0.24.0 cut gate was red (run 44362577581). A red cut gate costs about 53 minutes and blocks the tag.

What happens:
- A heavy lane is either skipped (per patch) or run in full (at the cut). There is nothing between the two.

Expected:
- A light variant of each heavy test: a smaller fixture or a reduced set, a few minutes in total. It runs at review and merge time (see the issue about reachable heavy tests).
- The light variant is added next to the full test. The `#[test]` count does not go down, and the golden asserts stay in the ignored set.
- A red light run is a note on the PR. It names the red steps and says: run the full heavy lane for these steps locally (`--only` or `--failed`).
- The author runs the full heavy steps locally, in release mode, and they must pass before the cut gate starts again.

body:
Asked for by Mike (collaborator) on 2026-11-18: SolidCraft shows "update available" in its title bar; a click downloads the latest version and installs it. CamCraft has nothing like it - a user only finds a new release on GitHub.

Wanted:
1. **Check:** at start (and at most once a day), read the latest release tag from GitHub (`api.github.com/repos/NeoTech/Camcraft/releases/latest`). No account, no telemetry; a setting turns it off; offline or rate-limited = silent, never an error dialog. Never in the browser (wasm) build.
2. **Show:** a small "Update available: vX.Y.Z" item at the right of the title bar, next to the version (#352). Its tooltip names the version and links the release notes.
3. **Install on click** - the hard part, because the app is running:
   - Download the asset for this platform (Windows zip/installer, macOS, Linux tar/AppImage, FreeBSD) to a temp folder and check its SHA-256 against the release (the release needs a checksum file - today it has none) before anything runs.
   - Unsaved work: ask to save first (the usual unsaved-changes prompt); never drop work.
   - Replace and restart: a running exe cannot be overwritten on Windows. Usual pattern: quit, let a small helper (or the installer itself) swap the files and start the new version; or rename the running exe aside and put the new one in place, then restart. Package-manager installs (AUR, Homebrew, a .deb) are not self-updated: show "update available" with the command to run instead.
   - Failure at any step leaves the old version working and says what failed.
4. Never auto-install without a click; never download in the background without the setting allowing it.

Done means: on Windows and one of macOS/Linux, a build that is one release behind shows "Update available", a click updates it and restarts on the new version with the project reopened; a corrupt download (bad checksum) is refused with a message and the old version still starts; with the setting off or offline, nothing is shown and nothing fails.

Clean-room note: this is ordinary desktop-app behaviour (no Autodesk material involved). SolidCraft (our sister project) is a reference for the user experience only.

title: Process: test merge batches before they reach main, and make a release cut take about an hour (v0.22.0 took about 6 h)

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:build
labels.description: Build, CI, release, tests

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P5
labels.description: Agent surface and tooling keep up with what shipped

body:
Asked for by the maintainer's collaborator (2026-11-16, after the v0.22.0 cut): "This should be smooth and quick. Pull all processing before the merge to main if possible. Velocity Velocity Velocity". These are proposals for the maintainer to decide. Nothing here changes a process file yet.

## What happened on 2026-11-16

| Phase | Time | Cause |
|---|---|---|
| Merge stop to release branch | about 3.5 h | `main` did not compile (#2143, from #1753), a red test (#2137), a P1 found during the cut (#2152), and a P2 with two competing fix PRs (#2004: #2013 and #2141) |
| Release gate (`cut.yml`) | 1.6 h | the full release tier in one job on one runner |
| Merge, tag, `release.yml` | about 1 h | package builds on hosted runners |

Later the same day `main` went red two more times (#2198, #2244). Each time, two PRs that passed alone did not build or pass together (#2244: #2140 and #2077). The post-merge gate found each one, but only after the merge.

## Proposals

1. **Test the batch before the merge (a merge queue).** Before a merge batch, build a candidate: `main` plus every PR of the batch, merged in the `merge-plan` order. Run the batch tier on the candidate. Merge the batch only when the candidate is green. If it is red, remove the PR that breaks it and test again. The post-merge gate then only confirms. (mkinney's coordinator does this on its own machines from today, with the user's yes for each PR.)
2. **Check `main` on each new commit.** A fast compile check (clippy on all crates, `--all-targets`) and `cargo test -p xtask` take about 2 to 5 minutes with a warm cache. A failure names the merge within the hour. (mkinney's coordinator runs this hourly from today; it found #2244.)
3. **A cut-readiness verdict before "cut".** Before the merge stop: no open P1 or P2, no open release PR, the compile check and the batch tier green on that exact `main` sha, and the packaging dry run green. The result is one line: GO or NO-GO with the reasons.
4. **Reuse a green rehearsal at the cut.** Run the release tier nightly on `main`. If `release/vX.Y.Z` differs from a rehearsed sha only by release notes, `CHANGELOG.md`, `RECOMMENDED.md` and the version bump, `cut.yml`'s gate stage accepts the rehearsal result (the same "gated tree is the tagged tree" check that the tag stage makes). Saves about 1.5 h.
5. **Split the release tier across runners.** The heavy lanes are independent. Run them as parallel jobs on the self-hosted runners (uma, m3 and others), then join the results. About 1.6 h becomes about 30 min when a full run is necessary.
6. **Measure `release.yml`.** Find the slowest job (probably macOS) and check the cache and split options.
7. **One fix for one P1/P2.** No second fix PR for an issue that already has one, and a known gap in a P1/P2 fix is fixed on the branch, not left as a note (the cause of #2152).

Target: a cut from GO to published release in about 1 hour, and `main` green between cuts.

## Open questions for the maintainer

- Accept 1 for all collaborator merges (the repository `merge-ready` skill would build and test the candidate before it merges)?
- Accept 4 and 5 for `cut.yml` (a process change, with a `PROCESS_VERSION` bump)?
- Which runner runs the nightly rehearsal (3 and 4)?

Done means: the maintainer decides each proposal on this issue, and each accepted one gets its own sub-issue.

title: Research: open and simulate a G-code file (any .nc, not only CamCraft's own toolpaths)

labels.name: enhancement

labels.name: area:sim

labels.name: area:post
labels.description: Post processors and G-code

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: needs-research
labels.description: Large idea with open questions: research and file sub-issues before any code

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

labels.name: P8
labels.description: Larger idea needing design or research before code

body:
Asked on Discord (2026-11-16): "Are we going to do a trajectory simulation? Something like CAMotics?" The maintainer's collaborator wants it: "Yes open ticket, I would like that".

## What is missing

CamCraft simulates the toolpaths that it generates: stock removal, playback, and the tool, holder, fixture and machine-travel laws (#2181, #2193, #2194 improve the playback). It cannot open a G-code file and simulate it. Examples of files that users want to check:
- a program from a different CAM program;
- a hand-written or edited program;
- a CamCraft program that was edited after the post.

## Wanted

Open an `.nc` / `.tap` / `.gcode` file, select the machine (and with it the dialect), and simulate it with the existing stock simulation and verify laws: material removal, gouges against an optional model, collisions with the holder and fixtures, and travel limits. The result is the same view and the same findings as for CamCraft's own toolpaths.

## Open questions (research)

1. **Reader.** A G-code reader for each supported dialect (Fanuc, Haas, Tormach/LinuxCNC, grblHAL, Heidenhain conversational, Siemens, Mazak, Doosan, Sodick wire...). Which words are read: modal groups, G90/G91, G20/G21, arcs (I/J/K and R), planes G17/G18/G19, canned cycles (expanded to moves), tool changes (T/M6 and the tool length offset), work offsets, G28/G30/G53, subprograms and macros. What is refused by name.
2. **Tools.** How a file's tool numbers map to CamCraft tools: the machine's tool table, the document's tool library, or a prompt for each T number.
3. **Setup.** Stock, work offset and fixtures: taken from the open document, or entered with the file.
4. **Multi-axis.** 4th and 5th axis words, through the machine kinematics (the AC solver of #2056 in reverse).
5. **Units and errors.** A word that the reader does not understand gives a clear refusal with the line number, never a silent skip.
6. **Use of it.** A "compare" mode: post a CamCraft program, then read it back and simulate it, so that the post is checked end to end (a round-trip test for every built-in post).
7. **Where it lives.** A reader crate beside `camcraft-post` (domain only), with the open-file command and its MCP tool in `app`.

## Clean room

Specify the reader from public sources only: the G-code standards (RS-274/NGC, ISO 6983), the controls' published programming manuals, and our own post scripts. Do not read or adapt the code of CAMotics, LinuxCNC's interpreter or other G-code simulators. Do not use programs that Fusion 360 or HSMWorks generated as test input.

## Done means

The open questions are answered in comments on this issue, and the concrete sub-issues are filed (each with one `P*`, one `effort:*`, `area:*`, `source:agent`, a "Done means" line and "Part of #N"), linked back here. Then `needs-research` is dropped and this umbrella closes.

title: Research: automatic nesting - place 2D parts on a sheet to minimise waste, with cut side and cut order

labels.name: area:2d

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: needs-research
labels.description: Large idea with open questions: research and file sub-issues before any code

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

labels.name: P8
labels.description: Larger idea needing design or research before code

body:
Asked for by the user (2026-11-16, in chat), after comparing CamCraft with WAZER's WAM software, which "requires closed paths" and "does not do nesting":

> "By nesting, I mean here are parts, figure out how to optimally place them so I can minimize material waste"

> "I'd suspect the workflow would be to open the models (probably svg and dxf files, enter material info (dimensions, type, thickness), kerf and minimal space between cuts, and you'd press a button to have it do layout. WAM had options to do inside, on line, or outside line cutting. The cutting logic gets tricky because you have to do some cuts (like internal features) first"

## What is missing

CamCraft has no automatic nesting: there is no way to give it a set of 2D parts and a sheet and have it place the parts to waste as little material as possible. `#1447` (common-line cutting in a nest) assumes the parts are already placed.

## Wanted workflow (from the user)

1. Open the part drawings: SVG (`#1880`) and DXF (`#1452`, `#1865`), several files, with a quantity per part.
2. Enter the sheet: width x height, material type, thickness.
3. Enter the kerf and the minimum gap between cuts (and from the sheet edge).
4. Choose the cut side per part or per profile: inside, on the line, or outside the line.
5. Press one button: CamCraft lays out the parts on the sheet (and on more sheets if they do not fit), and shows the use of material.
6. The cut order follows from the layout: internal features (holes) before the part outline, small parts before the parts around them, and no part cut free while a later cut still needs it.

## Open questions (research)

1. **Algorithm.** True-shape nesting from published literature, for example no-fit polygons (Bennell and Oliveira, "The geometry of nesting problems: a tutorial", EJOR 2008; Burke et al., "Complete and robust no-fit polygon generation for the irregular stock cutting problem", EJOR 2007) with a bottom-left fill or a local-search placement order. Which method, what run time is acceptable, and is the result deterministic (same input, same layout)?
2. **Rotations and mirroring.** Free rotation, fixed steps (0/90/180/270 or 15 degrees), or locked (grain direction, a printed face)? Mirroring allowed?
3. **Spacing.** How the kerf, the minimum gap, leads and pierce points enter the spacing (offset each part by half the kerf plus half the gap before nesting?). The sheet edge margin, and holes or scrap areas already in the sheet (a remnant).
4. **Parts in holes.** May a small part be placed inside a large part's hole?
5. **Document model.** Is a nest a new entity (sheet + placed part instances) with undoable commands (`CreateNest`, `EditNest`, `RunNesting`) and their MCP tools (AGENTS.md "Everything Is a Command" and "Commands ship with an MCP tool")? How does it relate to setups and stock?
6. **Cut order.** Holes before outlines; inside-out for parts inside holes; the "no part drops before its remaining cuts" rule shared with `#1447`; which machine kinds (waterjet, plasma, laser, router sheet jobs).
7. **Cut side.** Inside / on / outside the line per profile, mapped onto the 2D profile and waterjet operations (`#1883`), with open paths handled where the operation allows (WAM cannot cut open paths).
8. **Output.** Material use (percent), the waste outline, and a sheet count.

## Clean room

Specify from published literature and our own design notes only. Do not read or adapt nesting code or other CAM programs' internals (Fusion, HSMWorks, WAM's JavaScript, SVGnest, Deepnest and the like are not sources). The user's own WAM projects (G-code beside `.wzr` files, which the user cleared for reading) may be used only to compare CamCraft's output on the same parts.

## Done means

The open questions are answered in comments on this issue, and the concrete sub-issues are filed (each with one `P*`, one `effort:*`, `area:*`, `source:agent`, a "Done means" line and "Part of #N"), linked back here; then `needs-research` is dropped and this umbrella closes.

Related: `#1447` (common-line cutting in a nest), `#1883` (waterjet profile operation), `#1886` (WAZER machines and post), `#1880` (SVG import), `#1452` (DXF import), `#1861` (outer vs hole chaining).

labels.description: Larger idea needing design or research before code

body:
Design 5-axis kinematics and Haas NGC multi-axis posting for trunnion tables (`TR160`, `TR210`, `TRT100`) and universal machining centers (`UMC-500`).

Public Haas specifications and codebase behavior expose these open problems:
- **Kinematics mismatch in CamCraft:** `crates/cl/src/cl/pose.rs:53` (`axis_to_angles`) outputs `[A, B, 0.0]` with `C` always zero, and `crates/app/src/machine/judge.rs:79-105` checks literal rotary letters without inverse kinematics. A `UMC-500` uses `B` (+120° to -35°) plus `C` (360°), which fails when any Y-tilted pose requests `A`. A `TR160`/`TRT100` calls its cradle `A` (±120°) and platter `B` (360°), where platter `B` turns perpendicular to tilted `A` rather than around static Y.
- **NGC 5-axis G-codes and options:** Haas NGC uses `G254`/`G255` (Dynamic Work Offset) for 3+2 indexing and `G234` (Tool Center Point Control, not Fanuc `G43.4`) for simultaneous 4/5-axis cutting. Both `G254` and `G234` are paid options (`haascnc.com`); controls without TCPC require `G93` inverse-time feed (`F = 1 / minutes` per move).
- **Brakes and limits:** 4th-axis (`M10`/`M11`) and 5th-axis (`M12`/`M13`) brakes clamp during indexed cuts and stay released (`M11`/`M13`) during simultaneous motion.

Deliver a design decision in `docs/decisions/` covering:
1. Inverse kinematics or kinematic-chain representation in `cl`/`judge.rs` for `B+C` UMCs and `A+B` trunnions (`TR160`/`TRT100`).
2. Option-gating rules in `.mch` and `haas.cps` for `G254`/`G255` (DWO), `G234` (TCPC), `G93` fallback, and `M10`–`M13` brakes.
3. Concrete implementation sub-issues for machine definitions, IK checks, and `haas.cps` 5-axis output.

Done means: A design decision in `docs/decisions/` defines the kinematic model, option gating, and implementation split for Haas 5-axis support.

title: macOS: sign and notarize the release app so Gatekeeper opens it without a workaround

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:build
labels.description: Build, CI, release, tests

labels.name: in-review
labels.description: Fix pushed on a branch with an open PR; merges at the next cut

labels.name: effort:medium
labels.description: One module or crate, a known pattern (issue-worker-medium)

labels.name: P6
labels.description: Accepted enhancement, not scheduled

body:
### What are you trying to do

Open CamCraft on a Mac after downloading it from the releases page, without having to override Gatekeeper.

The macOS app is ad-hoc signed and not notarized (`scripts/package-macos.sh`: "Distribution signing and notarization can replace this when credentials exist"). A browser download gets the quarantine flag, and macOS then blocks the first launch because Apple can't verify the developer. Every new release is a new copy, so a user has to override Gatekeeper again after each update.

The README says the first launch "may require Control-click → Open". Since macOS 15 (Sequoia) that no longer works for an app that isn't notarized: the user has to try to open it, then go to System Settings › Privacy & Security and click Open Anyway, or run `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/CamCraft.app` in Terminal.

### How you imagine it working

The release signs the macOS app with a Developer ID certificate and notarizes it, so it opens like any other downloaded app. It would work the same way Windows signing does now (`scripts/sign.ps1`):

- `scripts/package-macos.sh` signs with Developer ID (hardened runtime, secure timestamp) when signing credentials are configured through the environment, and keeps today's ad-hoc signature, with a printed "unsigned" line, when they aren't. Unsigned stays a valid release.
- When credentials are configured, the release job submits the ZIP or DMG with `xcrun notarytool submit --wait`, then staples the ticket to the app and the DMG with `xcrun stapler staple`.
- The certificate and the notary credentials (an App Store Connect API key, or an Apple ID with an app-specific password) live in repository secrets, as the Windows PFX does.

This needs an Apple Developer Program membership, so whether and when to do it is the maintainer's call. A smaller step that helps meanwhile: update the README's macOS line to the macOS 15 steps above.

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

body:
Asked for by the maintainer (2026-11-13, in chat): "we should be able to set start points on generated path and also exit points.. So the path gets regenerated to those."

What is missing: where an operation starts cutting and where it leaves is chosen by the generator alone. The user cannot say "enter here" or "leave here", for example to keep the entry mark off a visible face, to start a contour away from a clamp, or to end next to the following feature.

Wanted: on the operations where it has a meaning (2D Contour, Pocket, Adaptive, Face, Slot, Bore, and the 3D finishing passes that have a free start), two optional picks:
- Start point(s): picked in the viewport (a point on the model, a sketch point or typed coordinates). For a closed contour the path is re-sequenced to begin at the pick's nearest point on the chain, with its lead-in there; for a pocket or adaptive region the entry (helix, ramp or plunge) is placed at the pick. One pick per chain or region; chains with no pick keep the automatic choice.
- Exit point(s): the same for where the pass ends and the lead-out is placed.

Changing a pick is an undoable command (it edits the operation parameters) and regenerates the path. MCP: the same parameters on the operation tools.

Safety: a pick is a wish, never an override of a check. If the entry, lead or ramp at the picked place does not fit (helix does not fit in the region, lead-in gouges a wall, the point is outside the machinable region or inside a keep-out or fixture), the operation is refused by name or marked incomplete, saying which pick and why; it never moves the entry silently and never posts a path that the collision or gouge checks would refuse at the automatic entry.

Related: the companion issue on pre-drilled holes as entry positions (filed with this one).

Done means: a closed 2D contour with a picked start begins and leads in at that point and, with a picked exit, leads out there (golden CL); a pocket enters at its picked point; an impossible pick is refused by name in a test; undo and redo restore the previous path; the MCP tools take the picks; the structural UI test covers the two pick rows.

title: Adaptive plans differ across platforms on the same commit (likely libm last-place rounding)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: area:3d
labels.description: 3D milling and finishing

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

labels.name: P7
labels.description: Owed polish and small fixes

body:
Found while working #984.

**What happens:** the same commit plans the same part differently on two platforms. `app pocket3d_hsm::the_users_bore_roughs_adaptive_level_by_level_and_verifies_clean` (release) on ecb54b7f:

| platform | rings levels | moves / planar / arcs |
|---|---|---|
| Windows (the #850 measure, PR #865) | Z 20.000 | 5530 / 5497 / 600 |
| macOS, Apple silicon (Homebrew rustc 1.99.1) | Z 20.000 (crossing at -2.33, -2.78) | 5786 / 5753 / 651 |

macOS is deterministic run to run, so it is not hash-map order. Rust does not contract `a*b+c` into FMA unless asked, so the most likely cause is the platform libm: `f64::sin`, `cos`, `atan2`, `hypot`, `exp`, `powf` call the system math library (MSVC CRT, glibc, Apple libm), which are not correctly rounded and differ in the last place. The STEP tessellation and the adaptive planner both use them, and the planner's crossing and acceptance tests are knife edges a 16 nm change flips (#882, #982). Not yet confirmed which call sites diverge, and not run on Linux.

**Why it matters:** a toolpath (and so the posted G-code) for the same part, tool and parameters depends on the OS the user runs. Every output is still verified and a crossing plan is refused by name, so this is not a gouge; but golden counts and exact plan pins cannot hold across platforms, and a user can see a different path from the same project file on two machines.

**Possible directions (open):** route the geometry and planner transcendental calls through a pure-Rust deterministic libm (the `libm` crate is already in Cargo.lock) so every platform rounds the same; or make the planner's decisions robust to sub-micron perturbation (#882, #982). Either changes toolpaths and needs every adaptive fixture re-measured.

Done means: the cause is confirmed on a second platform (Windows or Linux run of the bore test, plus which calls diverge), and either the output is made platform-identical with goldens re-measured, or the decision not to is recorded.

Refs #984, #882, #982.
